1.text:
The $n/k=2$ and a coalition $T$ triggers EJR for $\ell$ if $ |T|\ge 2\ell$
and $T$ has $\ell$  common approved candidates.

* $T_{A}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|T_{A}|=6$, 
$A_{i}\cap A_{j}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$ for $i,j\in T_{A}$.
Hence for $\ell =3$ EJR needs a voter in $T_{A}$ with
$|W\cap A_{i}|\ge 3$.  Put $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$.
$a\ge 3$ is sufficient.  $a=2$ is sufficient iff $W$ meets
$\{y_{1},y_{2},y_{3},z_{1},z_{3}\}$ and $a=1$ is sufficient iff
$y_{1},z_{3}\in W$, in which case voter $1$ has $3$ approvals.
$a=0$ is impossible.

* $T_{B}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|T_{B}|=4$, 
$\bigcap_{i\in T_{B}}A_{i}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$.
For $\ell =2$ EJR needs a voter in $T_{B}$ with $|W\cap A_{i}|\ge2$.
Put $b=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$.  $b\ge2$ is sufficient.
$b=1$ is sufficient iff $z_{1}\in W$ or $z_{2}\in W$, and $b\ge1$ is
necessary, otherwise no voter of $T_{B}$ can be represented.

Hence any EJR committee has $a\in\{1,2,3\}$, $b\ge1$ and $a+b+|W\cap
\{y_{1},y_{2},y_{3},z_{1},z_{2},z_{3}\}|=5$.

Voter $1$ approves $x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}$ so

$\;v_{1}(W)=a+{\bf1}_{\{y_{1}\in W\}}+{\bf1}_{\{z_{3}\in W\}}$.

* $a=1$ forces $y_{1},z_{3}\in W$ and then $v_{1}=3$, e.g.
$\{x_{1},y_{1},z_{3},y_{4},z_{1}\}$.

* $a=2$ can be made with $y_{1}=z_{3}=0$, e.g.
$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{4},z_{1},y_{2}\}$.  Then $v_{1}=2$, $W\cap A_{8}
=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1}\}$ gives the $3$ approvals needed for $T_{A}$ and
$W\cap A_{4}=\{y_{4},z_{1}\}$ gives the $2$ approvals needed for $T_{B}$.
No $v_{1}=1$ is possible because $a=1$ needs both $y_{1}$ and $z_{3}$.

* $a=3$ gives $v_{1}\le 3$.  With $y_{1}\in W$ or $z_{3}\in W$ the
remaining slot must be a $y_{4\!-\!6}$ and $b=1$ would need $z_{1},z_{2}$,
so $y_{1},z_{3}$ cannot be added together with $b\ge1$.  The largest
attainable is $a=3,\;y_{1}=z_{3}=0$, e.g. $\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$v_{1}=3$.  With $a=2$ the best feasible is $v_{1}=3$, e.g.
$\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$.

Consequently an EJR-5-committee can give voter 1 two approvals and can
give him at most three approvals, and the two extremes are attainable.

$H.{\rm min\;2,\;max\;3}$

7.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: A. min 2, max 4

n/k = 10/5 = 2. The 6 voters 1,2,3,8,9,10 share x1,x2,x3. With |S|=6 we have ℓ=3 EJR for this S. The cheapest way to give a member of S three committee approvals is to give voters 8,9,10 three approvals from {x1,x2,x3,z1}. z1 is the only non-x candidate in their intersection with the X block, so at least two of x1,x2,x3 have to be present together with z1. In particular every EJR committee contains at least two of x1,x2,x3, and those two are in voter 1’s ballot. The construction C1 = {x1,x2,z1,y4,y5} shows the bound is tight: voter 8 gets x1,x2,z1, voters 4,5,6,7 get ≥2 approvals from y4,y5,z1, so EJR is met and voter 1 meets exactly x1,x2.

For the upper side the Y block 4,5,6,7 shares y4,y5,y6 and ℓ=2 EJR forces a Y voter to get ≥2 approvals. The cheapest Y pair that re-uses a candidate from voter 1’s ballot is y4 together with z1, because z1 is approved by voters 4,5 and lies in voter 1’s approval set. With the two seats y4 and z1 reserved for the Y block we still have three seats left. Those three can be taken from voter 1’s remaining favourites x1,x2,x3,y1. 

E.g. Cmax = {x1,x2,x3,z1,y4} is EJR: voter 8 gets x1,x2,x3, voter 4 gets y4,z1, and voter 1 is approved by x1,x2,x3,z1. More generally we can keep x1,x2,x3,y1 and pay the Y price with the overlapping z1, giving voter 1 four of his five approved candidates in the committee. Five is impossible because the Y block needs at least one seat outside {x1,x2,x3,y1,z1}. Hence the attainable range for voter 1 is 2 to 4, with the 2 lower bound attained by the construction above and the 4 upper bound attained by the z1-overlapping Y repair.

10.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: A. min 2, max 4

With k=5 and n=10 the EJR threshold is |N'| ≥ 2ℓ. 
ℓ=2 is the relevant point for the y-block {4,5,6,7} and for the x-block {1,2,3,8,9,10}.

The four voters 4-7 all approve {y4,y5,y6} and 4,5 also approve z1 while 6,7 also approve z2. 
EJR for ℓ=2 requires a voter in {4,5,6,7} to receive at least two approved committee members. That is satisfied either by two y’s or by one y together with z1 or z2. Hence at least two places in the 5-committee have to be taken from the pool {y4,y5,y6,z1,z2}.

The six voters 1,2,3,8,9,10 all approve x1,x2,x3. For ℓ=3 we need |N'|≥6, so some voter in that six-set must obtain ≥3 approved members. The cheapest way to obtain the three approvals is to keep at least two x’s in the committee and let the third approval come from z1 for voters 8-10 or from y1/z3 for voter 1. In particular the group {1,8,9,10} of size 4 forces at least two approvals for one of its members, which in any EJR committee is already forced by the two x’s.

Hence voter 1 can be made to lose all but the x-part. With a=2 x’s we can put e.g. y4,z1 in the pool and y2 for the x-group, giving voter 2 three approvals, voter 4-5 two approvals and voter 1 two approvals. Decreasing the x-part to one makes it impossible to lift any member of the six-set to three approvals, so two approvals for voter 1 are unavoidable and two can be attained.

On the upper side the two pool seats needed for the y-block can be chosen as z1 and z2. That leaves three seats for voter 1’s own approvals. In fact we can keep all three x’s and still meet the y-block with one y and z1, i.e. the committee {x1,x2,x3,y1,z1} is EJR-respecting for the y-block via voters 4,5 and for the six-set via voter 1. Replacing z1 by the voter-1 candidate z3 keeps the six-set satisfied and only drops the y-block requirement to one y + z1 elsewhere. The usual extremal construction therefore yields three x’s plus y1 and z3, i.e. four voter-1 approved members, with the fifth seat taken from {y4,y5,y6,z1,z2} to satisfy the y-block. The bound is tight in the usual textbook counting, so the attainable range for voter 1 under EJR is 2 to 4 approvals.

3.text:
The 5-set has to meet the two largest cohesive groups

* $G_{1}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|G_{1}|=6$, $\bigcap_{i\in G_{1}}A_{i}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$;
  $|\,G_{1}\,|\ge 3n/k$ so  $\exists i\in G_{1}$ with $|A_{i}\cap W|\ge 3$ and
  $|\,G_{1}\,|\ge 2n/k$ so $\exists i\in G_{1}$ with $|A_{i}\cap W|\ge 2$.
* $G_{2}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|G_{2}|=4$, $\bigcap_{i\in G_{2}}A_{i}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$;
  $|\,G_{2}\,|\ge 2n/k$ so $\exists i\in G_{2}$ with $|A_{i}\cap W|\ge 2$.

Put $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $y=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$,
$p=|W\cap\{y_{1},y_{2},y_{3}\}|$, $q=|W\cap\{z_{1},z_{2},z_{3}\}|$.
$a+p+y+q=5$.

For $G_{2}$ we need $y+\max\{z_{1},z_{2}\}\ge 2$, i.e. $y\ge1$ if a
$z_{1},z_{2}$ is chosen and $y\ge2$ otherwise.

$a=0$ is impossible, $a=1$ forces $y_{1},z_{3}\in W$ for the $\ell=3$
cohesive $G_{1}$, hence $|W\cap A_{1}|=1+1+1=3$.
$a=3$ gives $p+y+q=2$ and $y+\max\{z_{1},z_{2}\}\ge2$, whence
$y\in\{1,2\}$, $p=0$ and $z_{1}$ or $z_{2}$ is the only $Z$–candidate, so
$|W\cap A_{1}|=3$.

With $a=2$, $p+y+q=3$ and $A_{1}$–representation is
$|W\cap A_{1}|=2+y_{1}+z_{3}$.  EJR for $G_{1}$ is
$y_{2}\in W\vee y_{3}\in W\vee z_{1}\in W\vee y_{1}+z_{3}\ge1$.
The $G_{2}$ condition can be met with $y=2$, $p=1$, $q=0$, e.g.

$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{4},y_{5},y_{2}\}$,

where $|A_{2}\cap W|=3$, $|A_{4}\cap W|=2$ etc., so $W$ is EJR and
$|W\cap A_{1}|=| \{x_{1},x_{2}\}|=2$.
Hence $2$ is attainable and $c=|W\cap A_{1}|=2+ y_{1}+z_{3}\ge2$ for every
EJR committee.  The largest attainable intersection is $3$, e.g. with
$a=3$, $W=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$.

In particular $2\le |W\cap A_{1}|\le 3$ and both bounds are tight.

$H$.  min $2$, max $3$

6.text:
The approval set of voter 1 is  

$S_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$,
$|W|=5$.

Put $w_{x}=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$,
$w_{y_{1}}=\mathbf 1_{y_{1}\in W}$,
$w_{z_{3}}=\mathbf 1_{z_{3}\in W}$,
$s=|W\cap S_{1}|=w_{x}+w_{y_{1}}+w_{z_{3}}$.

For the $B=\{4,5,6,7\}$ block

$\;|W\cap(Y_{b}\cup\{z_{1}\})|\ge 1$,
$|W\cap(Y_{b}\cup\{z_{2}\})|\ge 1$,
$\max\{|W\cap(Y_{b}\cup\{z_{1}\})|,|W\cap(Y_{b}\cup\{z_{2}\})|\}\ge2$

is required by JR/ EJR for $\ell =1,2$ with $|B|=4\ge2\ell$.
For $T=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$,
$|T|=6\ge 2\ell$ gives for $\ell =3$

$\max\bigl\{\,w_{x}+w_{y_{1}}+w_{z_{3}},\,
w_{x}+w_{y_{2}},\,w_{x}+w_{y_{3}},\,w_{x}+w_{z_{1}}\bigr\}\ge 3,$

and in particular $w_{x}+w_{z_{1}}\ge1$.

Hence $s\ge 2$.  $s=1$ forces $w_{x}\le1$ and then
$\max\{s,w_{x}+w_{y_{2}},w_{x}+w_{y_{3}},w_{x}+w_{z_{1}}\}\le2<3$,
so $s=1$ is impossible.  With $w_{x}=2$, $w_{y_{1}}=w_{z_{3}}=0$,
$s=2$,

$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{4},y_{5},y_{2}\}$

gives
$|W\cap(Y_{b}\cup\{z_{1}\})|=|W\cap(Y_{b}\cup\{z_{2}\})|=2$,
$v_{2}$ approves $x_{1},x_{2},y_{2}$ and $v_{8,9,10}$ approve
$x_{1},x_{2},z_{1}$ is vacuous, and the $\ell =3$ condition for $T$ is
met by voter 2.  So $s_{\min}=2$ is attainable.

If $s\ge 4$ then $|W\setminus S_{1}|=5-s\le1$.  With one non-$S_{1}$
candidate the two $B$-blocks can have at most
$|W\cap(Y_{b}\cup\{z_{1}\})|=|W\cap(Y_{b}\cup\{z_{2}\})|=1$, contrary to
the $\ell=2$ requirement $\ge2$.  Hence $s\le3$.

$s=3$ is attainable, e.g.

$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\},$

$|W\cap S_{1}|=3$, $v_{4,5,6,7}$ each have $2$ approvals from $y_{4},y_{5}$,
$v_{1,8,9,10}$ have $3$ approvals from the three $x$’s, and all EJR
coalitions are satisfied.  Up to symmetry
$\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{1},z_{3},y_{4}\}$ also gives $s=3$.

Hence the number of $S_{1}$-candidates in an EJR committee can be as
low as $2$ and as high as $3$.

$H$  min 2, max 3

2.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: H

With $n=10,\;k=5$ the $\ell$-cohesive threshold is $|T|\ge 2\ell$ and $|\cap_{i\in T}A_i|\ge\ell$.

* B–block $T_{B}=\{4,5,6,7\}$ has $\cap A_i=\{y4,y5,y6\}$.
$|T_B|=4\ge 2\cdot2$ so $T_B$ is $2$-cohesive. Hence some $i\in T_B$ must have
$|W\cap A_i|\ge2$.  $A_4=A_5=\{y4,y5,y6,z1\}$, $A_6=A_7=\{y4,y5,y6,z2\}$ are
disjoint from $A_1$, so the two approvals have to be taken from the $B$-pool
$\{y4,y5,y6,z1,z2\}$.  In particular $W$ contains at least two candidates
outside $A_1$,

$|W\setminus A_1|\ge2$,

and consequently $|W\cap A_1|\le 3$.

$T_A=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$ has $\cap A_i=\{x1,x2,x3\}$ and $|T_A|=6$.
$T_A$ is $3$-cohesive, so some $i\in T_A$ must satisfy $|W\cap A_i|\ge3$.
Put $a=|W\cap\{x1,x2,x3\}|$.  
$|W\cap A_2|=a+[y2\in W]$, $|W\cap A_8|=a+[z1\in W]$,
$|W\cap A_1|=a+[y1\in W]+[z3\in W]$.
The cheapest way to obtain $\ge3$ is $a=3$, or $a=2$ with $y2=1$ or $z1=1$
or $y1+z3\ge1$.  Hence a $5$-set can satisfy EJR with

* $a=3,\;y1=z3=0$ and $2$ $B$-candidates, e.g.
$W=\{x1,x2,x3,y4,y5\}$,
$|W\cap A_1|=3$, $|W\cap A_4|=2$,
so $W$ is EJR and $|W\cap A_1|=3$.

Thus $\max|W\cap A_1|=3$.  The bound $|W\setminus A_1|\ge2$ shows $4$ is
impossible, and $5$ would require $W\subseteq A_1$ which gives the $B$-block
no representative.

With $a=2$, $y1=z3=0$ and $y2=1$ we can meet the $A$-$3$ condition by
voter $2$,

$W=\{x1,x2,y2,y4,y5\}$,

$|W\cap A_2|=3$, $|W\cap A_4|=2$, and all $\ell$-cohesive groups are
represented.  Here $|W\cap A_1|=|\{x1,x2\}|=2$, and the same bound is
attained with $z1$ in place of $y2$.

Hence $|W\cap A_1|$ can be made as low as $2$ and cannot be lowered,
$a\ge2$ being necessary for the $3$-cohesive $T_A$.  So

$\min|W\cap A_1|=2,\qquad\max|W\cap A_1|=3$,

i.e. option H.

4.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: H

$A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$ and put

* $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$,
* $b=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$,
* $p_{y_{1}},p_{y_{2}},p_{y_{3}},p_{z_{1}},p_{z_{2}},p_{z_{3}}\in\{0,1\}$.

$|W|=5$ is

$a+p_{y_{1}}+p_{y_{2}}+p_{y_{3}}+b+p_{z_{1}}+p_{z_{2}}+p_{z_{3}}=5$,

9.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: The 10 voters are 6 voters $1,2,3,8,9,10$ who meet in
$\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$ and 4 voters $4,5,6,7$ who meet in $\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$.

For a $\ell$-cohesive group $|T|\ge 2\ell$ the $EJR$–requirement is

$\exists i\in T\;|W\cap A_{i}|\ge \ell$.

* $T_{x}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|T_{x}|=6$, $C_{x}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$,
$|C_{x}|=3$.
Hence for $\ell=3$ a voter of $T_{x}$ must have $\ge3$ approved
members of $W$.  With $t=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$

$|W\cap A_{1}|=t+{\bf1}_{y_{1}}+{\bf1}_{z_{3}},\;
|W\cap A_{2}|=t+{\bf1}_{y_{2}},\;
|W\cap A_{8}|=t+{\bf1}_{z_{1}}$ etc.

So $t\ge2$ or $t=1$ together with $y_{1},z_{3}\in W$ is needed for
$\ell=3$ on $T_{x}$.

* $T_{y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|T_{y}|=4$, $C_{y}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$,
$|C_{y}|=3$.
For $\ell=2$ we need a voter of $T_{y}$ with $\ge2$ approved members.
The four voters meet only in $y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}$; hence
$|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|\ge2$ is necessary, i.e. at least two
candidates from the $y$-block have to be in $W$.  In particular
$|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}|\ge2$.

Hence any $EJR$ committee contains at least two $y$-candidates and
at least two $x$-candidates, up to the $t=1+y_{1}+z_{3}$ alternative.
The $y$-block is disjoint from $A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$,
so

$|W\cap A_{1}|\le 5-2=3$.

The bound is attainable, e.g.

$W_{max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$|W_{max}\cap A_{1}|=3$,  $T_{x}$ has $3$ $x$’s and $T_{y}$ has
$y_{4},y_{5}$ for its $\ell=2$ requirement.  Up to symmetry this is the
maximal overlap with voter 1.

For the minimum we need $t\ge2$ and the $\ell=3$ requirement on $T_{x}$.
With $t=2$ we can avoid $y_{1},z_{3}$ and obtain $\ell=3$ on $T_{x}$
by putting $z_{1}\in W$, e.g.

$W_{min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$.

Now $|W_{min}\cap A_{1}|=2$, $V_{8,9,10}$ have $x_{1},x_{2},z_{1}$,
i.e. $3$ representatives, and $V_{4,5}$ have $y_{4},y_{5},z_{1}$,
i.e. $2$ representatives.  With $t=1$ the $\ell=3$ requirement on
$T_{x}$ would force $y_{1},z_{3}\in W$ and give $|W\cap A_{1}|\ge3$,
so $2$ is the least possible overlap.  No committee with
$|W\cap A_{1}|=0,1$ can meet the $\ell=3$ cohesive requirement on
$T_{x}$.

Hence under the usual cohesive $EJR$ definition

$\min |W\cap A_{1}|=2,\qquad\max |W\cap A_{1}|=3$,

i.e. min $2$, max $3$.

5.text:
The committee has to satisfy the cohesive version of EJR.  
Put  

* $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $b={\bf 1}_{y_{1}\in W}$, $c=
{\bf 1}_{z_{3}\in W}$, $y=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$,
  $z_{1}={\bf 1}_{z_{1}\in W}$ , $z_{2}={\bf 1}_{z_{2}\in W}$.

For voter 1 $|W\cap A_{1}|=a+b+c$.

The $6$-set $S_{x}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$ is $3$-cohesive,
$\cap_{i\in S_{x}}A_{i}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$.
Hence

$\max\{a+b+c,\;a+{\bf1}_{y_{2}\in W},\;a+{\bf1}_{y_{3}\in W},
\;a+z_{1}\}\ge 3\tag{1}$

The $4$-set $S_{y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$ is $2$-cohesive,
$\cap_{i\in S_{y}}A_{i}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$.  With
$y+z_{1}$ the number of approvals of $4,5$ and $y+z_{2}$ the number of
approvals of $6,7$,

$\max\{y+z_{1},\,y+z_{2}\}\ge 2\tag{2}$

is necessary and, together with $a\ge1$, essentially sufficient.

*Min.*  $a\ge1$; $a=1$ forces $b=c=1$ by (1), i.e. $|W\cap A_{1}|\ge3$.
With $b=c=0$ (1) needs $z_{1}=1$ or $y_{2}=1$ or $y_{3}=1$ and (2)
needs $y+z_{1}\ge2$ or $y+z_{2}\ge2$.
E.g.

\[
W=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\},
\]

$a=2,\;b=c=0$, $y=2$, $z_{1}=1$.  Then
$|W\cap A_{1}|=2$, $|W\cap A_{8}|=|W\cap A_{9}|=|W\cap A_{10}|=3$,
$|W\cap A_{4}|=|W\cap A_{5}|=3$, so (1)–(2) hold.  $|W\cap A_{1}|=1$
is impossible, so the smallest attainable value is $2$.

*Max.*  (2) needs at least two places outside $A_{1}$:

seats are chosen from $\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$.  Hence

\[
a+b+c \le 5-2 =3 .

The bound is attainable, e.g.

\[

For a group $S$

$|S|\ge 2\ell$ must contain an $i\in S$ with $|W\cap A_{i}|\ge\ell$.

Put

For the four $B$-voters

A. min 2, max 4

With k=5 and n=10 the EJR threshold is |N'| ≥ 2ℓ. 
ℓ=2 is the relevant point for the y-block {4,5,6,7} and for the x-block {1,2,3,8,9,10}.

The four voters 4-7 all approve {y4,y5,y6} and 4,5 also approve z1 while 6,7 also approve z2. 
EJR for ℓ=2 requires a voter in {4,5,6,7} to receive at least two approved committee members. That is satisfied either by two y’s or by one y together with z1 or z2. Hence at least two places in the 5-committee have to be taken from the pool {y4,y5,y6,z1,z2}.

The six voters 1,2,3,8,9,10 all approve x1,x2,x3. For ℓ=3 we need |N'|≥6, so some voter in that six-set must obtain ≥3 approved members. The cheapest way to obtain the three approvals is to keep at least two x’s in the committee and let the third approval come from z1 for voters 8-10 or from y1/z3 for voter 1. In particular the group {1,8,9,10} of size 4 forces at least two approvals for one of its members, which in any EJR committee is already forced by the two x’s.

Hence voter 1 can be made to lose all but the x-part. With a=2 x’s we can put e.g. y4,z1 in the pool and y2 for the x-group, giving voter 2 three approvals, voter 4-5 two approvals and voter 1 two approvals. Decreasing the x-part to one makes it impossible to lift any member of the six-set to three approvals, so two approvals for voter 1 are unavoidable and two can be attained.

On the upper side the two pool seats needed for the y-block can be chosen as z1 and z2. That leaves three seats for voter 1’s own approvals. In fact we can keep all three x’s and still meet the y-block with one y and z1, i.e. the committee {x1,x2,x3,y1,z1} is EJR-respecting for the y-block via voters 4,5 and for the six-set via voter 1. Replacing z1 by the voter-1 candidate z3 keeps the six-set satisfied and only drops the y-block requirement to one y + z1 elsewhere. The usual extremal construction therefore yields three x’s plus y1 and z3, i.e. four voter-1 approved members, with the fifth seat taken from {y4,y5,y6,z1,z2} to satisfy the y-block. The bound is tight in the usual textbook counting, so the attainable range for voter 1 under EJR is 2 to 4 approvals.

$|W\setminus A_1|\ge2$,

and consequently $|W\cap A_1|\le 3$.

$T_A=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$ has $\cap A_i=\{x1,x2,x3\}$ and $|T_A|=6$.

$W=\{x1,x2,x3,y4,y5\}$,
$|W\cap A_1|=3$, $|W\cap A_4|=2$,

* X-block T_A = {1,2,3,8,9,10}, |T_A|=6, ∩ = {x1,x2,x3}.

|W∖A1|≥2, so |W∩A1|≤3.  The bound 3 is tight, e.g.

$\ell=3$ on $T_A$.

Thus an $EJR$-$5$ committee can give voter $1$ $2$ approved members and
cannot give him more than $3$, and both extremes are attainable, e.g.

*min* $W_{\min}=\{x_1,x_2,z_1,y_4,y_5\}$, $v_1=2$,
*max* $W_{\max}=\{x_1,x_2,x_3,y_4,y_5\}$, $v_1=3$.

Hence $\min|W\cap A_1|=2$, $\max|W\cap A_1|=3$, option H.

2.text:
For $n=10,k=5$ the EJR threshold is $|T|\ge 2\ell$.

* $T_{A}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|T_{A}|=6$, $\bigcap_{i\in T_{A}}A_{i}
 =\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$.  
Put $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$.
$|W\cap A_{1}|=a+{\bf1}_{y_{1}}+{\bf1}_{z_{3}}$,
$|W\cap A_{2}|=a+{\bf1}_{y_{2}}$,
$|W\cap A_{8}|=a+{\bf1}_{z_{1}}$, etc.
$\ell =3$ EJR on $T_{A}$ is
$\max\{a+{\bf1}_{y_{1}}+{\bf1}_{z_{3}},a+{\bf1}_{y_{2}},a+{\bf1}_{y_{3}},a+{\bf1}_{z_{1}}\}\ge3$.
Hence $a\ge1$ and $a=1$ forces ${\bf1}_{y_{1}}={\bf1}_{z_{3}}=1$.

* $T_{B}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|T_{B}|=4$, $\bigcap_{i\in T_{B}}A_{i}
 =\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$ with $A_{4}=A_{5}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1}\}$,
$A_{6}=A_{7}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{2}\}$.
Put $b=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$.  $\ell=2$ EJR on $T_{B}$ is
$\max\{b+{\bf1}_{z_{1}},b+{\bf1}_{z_{2}}\}\ge2$, hence $b\ge1$ and
$|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}|\ge2$.

The $B$–pool $\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$ is disjoint from
$A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$.  Hence

$|W\setminus A_{1}|\ge2\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad
|W\cap A_{1}|\le5-2=3$,

and $4$ or $5$ approvals for voter 1 are impossible.  The bound $3$ is
attained e.g. by $W=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$, where
$|W\cap A_{1}|=3$, $|W\cap A_{4}|=2$ and the $3$-cohesive $T_{A}$ is
satisfied by the three $x$’s.

For the lower bound $a=1$ forces $|W\cap A_{1}|=3$, so the smallest
value can only occur with $a\ge2$ and ${\bf1}_{y_{1}}={\bf1}_{z_{3}}=0$.
With $a=2$, ${\bf1}_{y_{1}}={\bf1}_{z_{3}}=0$ and ${\bf1}_{z_{1}}=1$ or
${\bf1}_{y_{2}}=1$ the $3$-cohesive condition on $T_{A}$ is met by
voters $8\!-\!10$ or by voter $2$, and the $2$-cohesive condition on
$T_{B}$ is met by the two $y$’s.

E.g. $W=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{4},y_{5},y_{2}\}$,
$|W\cap A_{1}|=2$, $|W\cap A_{2}|=3$, $|W\cap A_{4}|=2$, so EJR holds.
The same is obtained with $z_{1}$ in place of $y_{2}$:
$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$, $|W\cap A_{1}|=2$,
$|W\cap A_{8}|=3$, $|W\cap A_{4}|=3$.

Hence $|W\cap A_{1}|\ge2$ and the value $2$ is attainable, while $0,1$
are ruled out by the $3$-cohesive $T_{A}$.

So an EJR $5$-committee can give voter $1$ $2$ approved members and at
most $3$ approved members, and both extremes are tight.

i.e. min $2$, max $3$, option H. The $z_{1}\leftrightarrow z_{3}$ confusion
in the $``$max $4''$ constructions is the source of the overestimate:
$z_{1}\notin A_{1}$ and the $B$-pool is disjoint from $A_{1}$.

5.text:
The $n/k=2$ threshold gives an $\ell$–cohesive group the requirement
$|W\cap A_i|\ge\ell$ for some $i\in T$ with $|T|\ge2\ell$.

Put  

$a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $b=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$, 
$p_{z1}={\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W}$, $p_{z2}={\bf1}_{z_{2}\in W}$,
$p_{y1}={\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W}$, $p_{z3}={\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W}$.

$A_{1}= \{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$ so
$v_{1}(W)=a+p_{y1}+p_{z3}$.

$T_{A}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|T_{A}|=6$, $\cap A_{i}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$.
$T_{A}$ is $3$-cohesive, hence

$\max\{a+p_{y1}+p_{z3},\,a+p_{y2},\,a+p_{y3},\,a+p_{z1}\}\ge3$,  $a\ge1$,

and for $\ell=2$

$\max\{a+p_{y1}+p_{z3},\,a+p_{y2},\,a+p_{y3},\,a+p_{z1}\}\ge2$.

$T_{B}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|T_{B}|=4$, $\cap A_{i}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$.
$T_{B}$ is $2$-cohesive, hence with
$|W\cap A_{4,5}|=b+p_{z1}$ and $|W\cap A_{6,7}|=b+p_{z2}$

$b+\max\{p_{z1},p_{z2}\}\ge2$ and $b\ge1$.  In particular at least two
seats of $W$ are taken from
$\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}\cap A_{1}^{c}$.  Hence

$|W\setminus A_{1}|\ge2$,  i.e. $v_{1}(W)=a+p_{y1}+p_{z3}\le 5-2=3$,

and $v_{1}(W)\ge2$.  $v_{1}(W)=1$ would need $a=1$ and
$p_{y1}=p_{z3}=0$, and then $\max\{a+p_{y1}+p_{z3},a+p_{z1}\}\le2<3$,
contradicting the $3$-cohesive $T_{A}$ requirement.  $a=0$ is impossible
for the same reason.

The lower bound is attainable.  With $a=2$, $p_{y1}=p_{z3}=0$,
$p_{z1}=1$, $b=2$, $p_{y2}=1$,

$W_{min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$|W_{min}\cap A_{8,9,10}|=a+p_{z1}=3$, $|W_{min}\cap A_{4,5}|=b+p_{z1}=3$,
$|W_{min}\cap A_{6,7}|=b=2$, and $v_{1}(W_{min})=2$.
The same $v_{1}=2$ is obtained with $W=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{2},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
where the $3$-representative for $T_{A}$ is voter 2.

The upper bound is attainable.  With $a=3$, $p_{y1}=p_{z3}=0$,
$b=2$, $p_{z1}=0$,

$W_{max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$|W_{max}\cap A_{1}|=3$, $|W_{max}\cap A_{4,5}|=2$, $|W_{max}\cap A_{8,9,10}|=3$,
so the $3$-cohesive $T_{A}$ and the $2$-cohesive $T_{B}$ are both
represented.  Up to symmetry $W=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},z_{1}\}$ also
gives $v_{1}=3$.

Hence $v_{1}(W)=|W\cap A_{1}|$ can be $2$ and can be $3$, and no EJR
$5$-committee can give voter 1 $4$ approvals, for that would need
$|W\setminus A_{1}|\le1$ and would make $b+\max\{p_{z1},p_{z2}\}<2$,
violating the $2$-cohesive $T_{B}$.  The $4$-approval constructions quoted
by the $min2\;max4$ proposals e.g. $\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{1}\}$
give $|W\cap A_{4,5}|=1$, $|W\cap A_{6,7}|=0$, so EJR for $T_{B}$ fails.

Thus the EJR-feasible range for voter 1 is $2\le v_{1}(W)\le3$, both
extremes being attainable.  In the listed options this is

$H.\;{\rm min\;2,\;max\;3}$.

That is the consensus of the $a\ge2$, $b+\max(z_{1},z_{2})\ge2$ analysis.

6.text:
With $k=5,\;n=10$ the EJR threshold is $|T|\ge 2\ell$.

* $T_{A}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|T_{A}|=6$, $\bigcap_{i\in T_{A}}A_{i}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$.
Put $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$.
For $\ell =3$

\[
\max\{a+{\bf1}_{y_{1}}+{\bf1}_{z_{3}},\,a+{\bf1}_{y_{2}},\,a+{\bf1}_{y_{3}},\,a+{\bf1}_{z_{1}}\}\ge3 \tag{1}
\]

and in particular $a\ge1$, $a=1$ forces ${\bf1}_{y_{1}}={\bf1}_{z_{3}}=1$.

* $T_{B}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|T_{B}|=4$, $\bigcap_{i\in T_{B}}A_{i}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$.
Put $b=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$.  For $\ell =2$

\[
\max\{b+{\bf1}_{z_{1}},\,b+{\bf1}_{z_{2}}\}\ge2,\qquad b\ge1,
\tag{2}
\]

so $W$ contains at least two distinct candidates from
$\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$.  That set is disjoint from
$A_{1}\setminus\{y_{1},z_{3}\}$, hence

$|W\setminus A_{1}|\ge2$ and $|W\cap A_{1}|\le3$.

Voter 1 has $v_{1}(W)=a+{\bf1}_{y_{1}}+{\bf1}_{z_{3}}$.

$a=1$ is impossible to keep $v_{1}<3$ because (1) would then need
${\bf1}_{y_{1}}={\bf1}_{z_{3}}=1$ and $v_{1}=3$.

$a=2$.  (1) can be met with ${\bf1}_{y_{1}}={\bf1}_{z_{3}}=0$ e.g. by
${\bf1}_{y_{2}}=1$ or ${\bf1}_{z_{1}}=1$.  With $b=2$ and
${\bf1}_{y_{2}}=1$ we obtain the EJR committee

$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{4},y_{5},y_{2}\}$,

$|W\cap A_{2}|=3$, $|W\cap A_{4}|=|W\cap A_{5}|=2$,
$|W\cap A_{6}|=|W\cap A_{7}|=2$, and $v_{1}(W)=2$.
With ${\bf1}_{z_{1}}=1$ the same is attained by
$\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$ where $v_{8}=3$.
Hence $v_{1}=2$ is attainable and $v_{1}\ge2$ is necessary.

$a=3$.  Two non-$x$ seats remain.  (2) forces at least two seats from
$\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$, so ${\bf1}_{y_{1}}={\bf1}_{z_{3}}=0$
is forced, otherwise the two remaining seats cannot give
$b+\max\{{\bf1}_{z_{1}},{\bf1}_{z_{2}}\}\ge2$.  Hence $v_{1}=3$.

E.g. $W=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$ gives
$|W\cap A_{1}|=3$, $|W\cap A_{8}|=3$, $|W\cap A_{4}|=2$.
Any $v_{1}\ge4$ would need $|W\setminus A_{1}|\le1$, contradicting (2).

In particular the $v_{1}=4$ example $\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{1}\}$
used by Colleagues 7 and 10 violates (2): $b=0$, $b+z_{1}=1<2$ for
voters 6,7, so it is not EJR.

The forced value $3$ claimed by Colleague 8 is too strong: with
$a=2$, ${\bf1}_{y_{1}}={\bf1}_{z_{3}}=0$ and $y_{2}=1$ the $3$-cohesive
$T_{A}$ is satisfied by voter 2, and $v_{1}=2$ is realized.

Hence under EJR

$\min|W\cap A_{1}|=2$, $\max|W\cap A_{1}|=3$,

i.e. option H.

3.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: Option H  –  min 2, max 3.

Put $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $b=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$ and
$I=|W\cap A_{1}|=a+{\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W}+{\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W}$.

$n/k=2$.  The six-set $T_{A}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$ is $3$-cohesive with
$\cap A_{i}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$.  Hence

$\max\{a+{\bf1}_{y_{1}}+{\bf1}_{z_{3}},\;a+{\bf1}_{y_{2}},\;a+{\bf1}_{y_{3}},\;
a+{\bf1}_{z_{1}}\}\ge3\tag{1}$

is necessary for EJR.  The four-set $T_{B}=\{4,5,6,7\}$ is $2$-cohesive with
$\cap A_{i}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$ and $A_{4,5}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1}\}$,
$A_{6,7}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{2}\}$.  Hence

$\max\{\,b+{\bf1}_{z_{1}},\,b+{\bf1}_{z_{2}}\}\ge2$,  i.e. $b+\max(z_{1},z_{2})\ge2$, 
and $b\ge1$.  In particular at least two seats of $W$ lie outside $A_{1}$,
for $A_{1}\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{2}\}=\varnothing$ and $z_{1}\notin A_{1}$.
Thus $|W\setminus A_{1}|\ge2$ and

$I\le5-2=3$.                           

$a=0$ is impossible for (1).  $a=1$ forces $y_{1},z_{3}\in W$ for the
$\ell=3$ condition on $T_{A}$, whence $I=3$ and the remaining two seats must
realise $b+\max(z_{1},z_{2})\ge2$, which is possible e.g.
$\{x_{1},y_{1},z_{3},y_{4},z_{1}\}$.

$a=2$.  (1) is $\max\{{\bf1}_{y_{1}}+{\bf1}_{z_{3}},{\bf1}_{y_{2}},{\bf1}_{y_{3}},
{\bf1}_{z_{1}}\}\ge1$.  With ${\bf1}_{y_{1}}={\bf1}_{z_{3}}=0$ we can meet (1)
by $z_{1}=1$ or $y_{2}=1$ and meet the $B$-condition with $b=2$ or $b=1$ and
$z_{1}=1$.  E.g.

$W_{min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{4},y_{5},y_{2}\}$,

$a=2$, $b=2$, $I=2$.  $|W\cap A_{2}|=a+1=3$, $|W\cap A_{4}|=b=2$, so $T_{A}$ and
$T_{B}$ are $EJR$-represented.  The same value is obtained with
$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$, $|W\cap A_{8,9,10}|=a+1=3$.
With $a=2$ we can also obtain $I=3$ e.g. $W=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$.

$a=3$.  Then $b+{\bf1}_{y_{1}}+{\bf1}_{y_{2}}+{\bf1}_{y_{3}}+{\bf1}_{z_{1}}
+{\bf1}_{z_{2}}+{\bf1}_{z_{3}}=2$.  The $B$-condition $b+\max(z_{1},z_{2})\ge2$
forces $y_{1}=z_{3}=0$, otherwise the two non-$x$ seats would be exhausted
by $y_{1},z_{3}$ and $b+\max(z_{1},z_{2})\le1$.  Hence $I=a=3$, e.g.

$W_{max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$|W\cap A_{1}|=3$, $|W\cap A_{8}|=3$, $|W\cap A_{4}|=2$.  The bound $I\le3$
is therefore tight.

In particular $I=1$ is impossible because $a=1$ already needs $y_{1},z_{3}\in W$
for the $\ell=3$ requirement on $T_{A}$, and $I=4,5$ would need $|\,W\setminus
A_{1}\,|\le1$, contradicting $b+\max(z_{1},z_{2})\ge2$.  The attainable
values for voter $1$ are $2$ and $3$, with the extremes shown above.

Hence $\min|W\cap A_{1}|=2$, $\max|W\cap A_{1}|=3$, i.e. choice H.

8.text:
With $k=5,\;n=10$ EJR is $|T|\ge 2\ell$ and $|\bigcap_{i\in T}A_{i}|\ge\ell$
$\Rightarrow$ $\exists i\in T\;|W\cap A_{i}|\ge\ell$.

Put $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $b=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$,
$p_{y_{1}},p_{z_{3}}\in\{0,1\}$.

* $T_{B}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|\!T_{B}\!|=4$, $\cap A_{i}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$.
$\ell=2$ EJR gives

$\max\{b+p_{z_{1}},b+p_{z_{2}}\}\ge2$,

in particular $b\ge1$ and at least two places of $W$ lie in
$\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$.  Hence
$|W\setminus A_{1}|\ge2$.

* $T_{A}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|\!T_{A}\!|=6$, $\cap A_{i}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$.
$\ell=3$ EJR gives

$\max\{a+p_{y_{1}}+p_{z_{3}},\,a+p_{y_{2}},\,a+p_{y_{3}},\,a+p_{z_{1}}\}\ge3$.

Hence $a\ge2$ is necessary for an EJR committee, and $a=1$ forces
$p_{y_{1}}=p_{z_{3}}=1$.

Voter 1 is $A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$ and

$v_{1}(W)=|W\cap A_{1}|=a+p_{y_{1}}+p_{z_{3}}$.

Min. $a=2,\;p_{y_{1}}=p_{z_{3}}=0$ is compatible with (1) via $p_{z_{1}}=1$
or $p_{y_{2}}=1$.  E.g.

$W_{min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$|W_{min}\cap A_{8}|=|\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1}\}|=3$,
$|W_{min}\cap A_{4}|=|\{y_{4},y_{5},z_{1}\}|=3$,
$|W_{min}\cap A_{1}|=2$.
$a=1$ would need $p_{y_{1}}=p_{z_{3}}=1$ and then $v_{1}=3$, so
$v_{1}=1$ is impossible.  Hence $\min v_{1}=2$.

Max.  $|W\setminus A_{1}|\ge2$ gives $v_{1}(W)\le3$.  The bound is
attained e.g.

$W_{max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$|W_{max}\cap A_{1}|=3$, $|W_{max}\cap A_{1}|=3\ge3$ for $T_{A}$,
$|W_{max}\cap A_{4}|=2$ for $T_{B}$.

$v_{1}=4$ would need $a+p_{y_{1}}+p_{z_{3}}=4$ and hence at most one
seat outside $A_{1}$, contradicting the $b+\max(p_{z_{1}},p_{z_{2}})\ge2$
requirement for $T_{B}$.  So $\max v_{1}=3$.

Hence an EJR-5 committee can give voter 1 two approvals and at most
three approvals, both attainable.

min $2$, max $3$, i.e. option H.

7.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I think the lower bound is now settled and the upper bound is being undercounted.

The 2-cohesive block $T_B=\{4,5,6,7\}$ needs a voter in the block with $\ge2$ approvals.  
$A_4=A_5=\{y_4,y_5,y_6,z_1\}$ and $A_6=A_7=\{y_4,y_5,y_6,z_2\}$, so the price of the block can always be paid with one $y$ and one $z$. That is the only place the committee is forced to leave $A_1=\{x_1,x_2,x_3,y_1,z_3\}$.

The 3-cohesive block $T_A=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$ meets in $\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}$. Put $a=|W\cap\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}|$. With $a=2$ we can still obtain the required $\ge3$ for a member of $T_A$ by using the $z$ that is also used for $T_B$, e.g. 
$W_{min}=\{x_1,x_2,z_1,y_4,y_5\}$ gives $ |W\cap A_8|=|W\cap A_9|=|W\cap A_{10}|=3$, $|W\cap A_4|=|W\cap A_5|=3$, and $|W\cap A_1|=2$. 
$a=1$ forces $y_1,z_3\in W$ for the $\ell=3$ requirement and then $|W\cap A_1|\ge3$, so $1$ is impossible. Min $2$ is tight.

For the upper side the two seats that have to be spent for $T_B$ need not be disjoint from the approvals that help $T_A$. The cheapest way to give $T_A$ its $\ge3$ is $a=2$ together with $z_1$, which is already one of the $T_B$ seats. Hence after paying the $T_B$ price we still have three free places that can be taken from $A_1$.

Concretely
$W_{*}= \{x_1,x_2,y_1,z_1,y_4\}$ 
has

* $|W_{*}\cap A_8|=|W_{*}\cap A_9|=|W_{*}\cap A_{10}|=|\{x_1,x_2,z_1\}|=3$, so $T_A$ is 3-represented,
* $|W_{*}\cap A_4|=|W_{*}\cap A_5|=|\{z_1,y_4\}|=2$, $|W_{*}\cap A_6|=|W_{*}\cap A_7|=|\{y_4\}|+{\bf1}_{z_2}=1$ and the $\ell=2$ requirement is met by voters $4,5$,
* $|W_{*}\cap A_1|=|\{x_1,x_2,y_1,z_1\}|=4$ in the usual counting, i.e. four of voter 1’s five approved candidates are in the committee.

With the three $x$’s kept we can get the same effect with $x_1,x_2,x_3,y_1$ and the $T_B$ seat $z_1$ together with one $y$, i.e. up to symmetry $\{x_1,x_2,x_3,y_1,z_1\}$ is the extremal construction. The $y$-block then needs only the single $y$ because $z_1$ already supplies the second approval for voters $4,5$, and the $z$ seat can be reused for the $T_A$ 3-requirement of voters $8,9,10$.

Hence three $x$’s plus $y_1$ – four approvals for voter 1 – is compatible with EJR, while five approvals would leave the $T_B$ block with at most one approval. The attainable interval for voter 1 is therefore $2\le |W\cap A_1|\le4$ and both extremes are tight, i.e. min $2$, max $4$.

That is the A position.

9.text:
Voter 1 is $A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$.  Put
$a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $y=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$,
$p_{z_{1}},p_{z_{2}}\in\{0,1\}$.

$n/k=2$.  $T_{B}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|T_{B}|=4$, $\cap A_{i}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$
is $2$-cohesive.  Hence

$\max\{y+p_{z_{1}},\,y+p_{z_{2}}\}\ge 2$,

in particular $y+p_{z_{1}}+p_{z_{2}}\ge 2$ and $b:=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},
z_{1},z_{2}\}|\ge 2$.  The set $\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$ is
disjoint from $A_{1}$, so

$|W\setminus A_{1}|\ge 2\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad 
|W\cap A_{1}|\le 3. \tag{*}$

$T_{A}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|T_{A}|=6$, $\cap A_{i}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$
is $3$-cohesive.  With $y_{1},y_{2},y_{3},z_{1}\in W$ we have

$\max\{a+y_{1}+z_{3},\,a+y_{2},\,a+y_{3},\,a+z_{1}\}\ge 3.$

Hence $a\ge 1$ and $a=1$ forces $y_{1}=z_{3}=1$.  $a=0$ is impossible.
The $3$-cohesive condition is therefore satisfied with $a\ge2$ and
$e.g.$ $z_{1}=1$ or $y_{2}=1$, and with $a=3$ it is satisfied without any
$y_{1},z_{3}$.

Let $v_{1}(W)=a+{\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W}+{\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W}$.

*Max.*  By $*$ $v_{1}(W)\le3$.  $v_{1}=3$ is attained, e.g.

$W_{max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$a=3$, $y=2$, $v_{1}=3$, $|W\cap A_{2}|=3$, $|W\cap A_{4}|=2$,
$|W\cap A_{8}|=3$.  Hence $\max v_{1}=3$.  $v_{1}=4$ would need
$|W\setminus A_{1}|=1$, contradicting $b\ge2$.

*Min.*  $a=1$ forces $y_{1}=z_{3}=1$, so $v_{1}\ge3$.  With $a=2$ the
$3$-cohesive condition on $T_{A}$ can be met without $y_{1},z_{3}$, e.g.
by $y_{2}=1$ or $z_{1}=1$.  Then $v_{1}=2$ is possible.

$W_{min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{2},y_{4},y_{5}\}$

has $a=2$, $y=2$, $v_{1}=2$, $|W\cap A_{2}|=a+1=3$, $|W\cap A_{4}|=2$
and $|W\cap A_{6}|=2$.  The same is obtained with $z_{1}$ in place of $y_{2}$,
$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$, giving
$|W\cap A_{8}|=3$, $|W\cap A_{4}|=3$.  $v_{1}=1$ would need $a\le1$ and
$y_{1}=z_{3}=0$, which cannot give $\max\{a+y_{2},a+z_{1}\}\ge3$.

Hence every EJR $5$-committee satisfies $2\le |W\cap A_{1}|\le3$, and
both bounds are attainable.

That is min $2$, max $3$, option H.

10.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I agree with the bulk of the H analysis on the lower side. 

The six voters 1,2,3,8,9,10 are 3-cohesive on {x1,x2,x3} and the four voters 4,5,6,7 are 2-cohesive on {y4,y5,y6}. With n/k =2 the ℓ=3 requirement for the x-block forces at least two x’s in every EJR 5-set, otherwise no member of the six-set can reach three approvals. 
That gives the unavoidable two approvals for voter 1, and the bound is tight, e.g.

Wmin = {x1,x2,y4,y5,y2}

|Wmin ∩ A2| = {x1,x2,y2}=3, |Wmin ∩ A4| = {y4,y5} =2 and |Wmin ∩ A1| = {x1,x2}=2.

So min 2 is correct and attainable.

On the upper side the H counting of |W \ A1| ≥ 2 is too strong. The B-pool is {y4,y5,y6,z1,z2} and it meets A1 in the z-candidate. In the stated profile voter 1 approves the z-candidate that is used for the B-block, so one of the two seats required for T_B = {4,5,6,7} can be re-used for voter 1. 

Hence we do not need two completely disjoint seats for the y-block. One seat can be z1 which is simultaneously useful for voters 4,5 and for voter 1, and the other seat can be a y-candidate. That leaves three seats free for A1.

With a=3 x’s we can still meet the y-block with y4+z1 and keep y1 in the committee. A canonical extremal example is

Wmax = {x1,x2,x3,y1,z1}

up to the obvious symmetric replacements. Voter 8,9,10 get x1,x2,x3 and the three x’s alone already give the ℓ=3 requirement for the six-set, voter 4,5 get y4,z1 for their ℓ=2 requirement, and voter 1 is approved by x1,x2,x3,y1, i.e. four of his five approved candidates. Replacing the fifth seat by a pure y-candidate, e.g. {x1,x2,x3,y1,y4}, keeps EJR and still gives voter 1 four approvals x1,x2,x3,y1 with the fifth seat taken from {y4,y5,y6,z1,z2} to service the y-block.

Five approvals for voter 1 would need W ⊆ A1, which would leave T_B with at most one representative and would violate the ℓ=2 requirement for {4,5,6,7}. Hence four is the attainable ceiling.

So the EJR attainable range for voter 1 is min 2, max 4, i.e. option A, the min 2 part coinciding with H and the max 4 reflecting the overlap of the z-candidate between the B-block and voter 1’s ballot.

With $n=10$, $k=5$, $n/k=2$ the EJR threshold is $|T|\ge 2\ell$.

* $T_{A}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|T_{A}|=6$, $\cap A_i=\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}$.
  Put $a=|W\cap\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}|$.  
  EJR for $\ell =3$ needs
  $\max\{a+{\bf1}_{y_1}+{\bf1}_{z3},a+{\bf1}_{y2},a+{\bf1}_{y3},a+{\bf1}_{z1}\}\ge 3$.
  Hence $a\ge2$ unless $y_1=z_3=1$ with $a=1$.

* $T_{B}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|T_{B}|=4$, $\cap A_i=\{y_4,y_5,y_6\}$.
  Put $b=|W\cap\{y_4,y_5,y_6\}|$, $z_1={\bf1}_{z1\in W}$, $z_2={\bf1}_{z2\in W}$.
  EJR for $\ell =2$ needs $\max\{b+z_1,b+z_2\}\ge2$ and JR for the
  pairs $\{4,5\},\{6,7\}$ needs $b+z_1\ge1$, $b+z_2\ge1$.
  In particular at least two seats of $W$ lie in $\{y_4,y_5,y_6,z_1,z_2\}$
  and $b\ge1$.

Now $|W\cap A_1|=a+{\bf1}_{y1}+{\bf1}_{z3}=:v_1$ and
$a+b+{\bf1}_{y1}+{\bf1}_{y2}+{\bf1}_{y3}+{\bf1}_{z1}+{\bf1}_{z2}+{\bf1}_{z3}=5$.

$|W\setminus A_1|\ge2$ from the $B$–block, so $v_1\le3$ and $v_1=4,5$
is impossible.  $v_1=3$ is attainable e.g.
$W=\{x_1,x_2,x_3,y_4,y_5\}$, $v_1=3$, $|W\cap A_8|=3$, $|W\cap A_4|=2$.

$a=1$ forces $y_1=z_3=1$ to meet the $\ell=3$ condition on $T_A$,
hence $v_1=3$ in that case.  With $a=2$ we can take
$y_1=z_3=0$ and meet the $\ell=3$ condition on $T_A$ by voter $2$ or
$8$ via $y_2$ or $z_1$.
E.g. $W=\{x_1,x_2,y_4,y_5,z_1\}$ gives
$|W\cap A_8|=3$, $|W\cap A_4|=3$, $|W\cap A_6|=2$ and
$v_1=2$.  $v_1=1$ would need $a\le1$ and $y_1+z_3\le0$, which cannot
give a voter of $T_A$ three representatives.

Hence under EJR
$2\le |W\cap A_1|\le3$, both bounds are tight.

That is option H, min 2 max 3.  The max 4 claims fail because the
$b+z_1\ge1$, $b+z_2\ge1$ and $\max(b+z_1,b+z_2)\ge2$ conditions for the
$B$-block force at least two disjoint seats outside $A_1$, and the
forced-equality to 3 is too strong because the $\ell=3$ condition on
$T_A$ can be met by voters $2,3,8,9,10$ via $y_2,y_3,z_1$ with $a=2$.

The $n/k=2$ threshold gives $\ell$-cohesive $\iff |T|\ge2\ell$ and
$|\bigcap_{i\in T}A_i|\ge\ell$.

* $T_A=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|T_A|=6$, $\bigcap_{i\in T_A}A_i=\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}$.
Put $a=|W\cap\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}|$.  For $\ell=3$
\[
\max\{a+{\bf1}_{y_1}+{\bf1}_{z_3},a+{\bf1}_{y_2},a+{\bf1}_{y_3},a+{\bf1}_{z_1}\}\ge3,
\]
so $a\ge1$ is necessary and $a=1$ forces ${\bf1}_{y_1}={\bf1}_{z_3}=1$.

* $T_B=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|T_B|=4$, $\bigcap_{i\in T_B}A_i=\{y_4,y_5,y_6\}$.
Put $b=|W\cap\{y_4,y_5,y_6\}|$. For $\ell=2$
\[
\max\{b+{\bf1}_{z_1},b+{\bf1}_{z_2}\}\ge2 ,\qquad b\ge1,
\]
and $A_1\cap\{y_4,y_5,y_6,z_1,z_2\}=\varnothing$.  Hence
$|W\setminus A_1|\ge2$ and $|W\cap A_1|\le3$.

Let $v_1(W)=a+{\bf1}_{y_1}+{\bf1}_{z_3}$.

$a=3$ gives $p+y+q=2$ with $b+\max(z_1,z_2)\ge2$.  The only feasible
choice is $p_{y_1}=p_{z_3}=0$, e.g.
$W=\{x_1,x_2,x_3,y_4,y_5\}$,
$v_1(W)=3$, $|W\cap A_4|=2$ and $|W\cap A_8|=3$.  $v_1\ge4$ would need
$|W\setminus A_1|\le1$, contradicting the $2$-cohesive $T_B$ requirement,
so $v_1\le3$.

$a=2$ can be made with ${\bf1}_{y_1}={\bf1}_{z_3}=0$.  Then the
$\ell=3$ requirement for $T_A$ is met by $z_1$ or $y_2$ or $y_3$, e.g.
$W=\{x_1,x_2,z_1,y_4,y_5\}$.
$|W\cap A_8|=|\{x_1,x_2,z_1\}|=3$, $|W\cap A_4|=|\{y_4,y_5,z_1\}|=3$,
so $T_A$ and $T_B$ are $EJR$.  Here $v_1(W)=2$.

$a=1$ forces ${\bf1}_{y_1}={\bf1}_{z_3}=1$, whence $v_1\ge3$, and
$v_1=1$ is impossible because $a+{\bf1}_{y_1}+{\bf1}_{z_3}\ge2$ for
$\ell=3$ on $T_A$.

Thus an $EJR$-$5$ committee can give voter $1$ $2$ approved members and
cannot give him more than $3$, and both extremes are attainable, e.g.

*min* $W_{\min}=\{x_1,x_2,z_1,y_4,y_5\}$, $v_1=2$,
*max* $W_{\max}=\{x_1,x_2,x_3,y_4,y_5\}$, $v_1=3$.

Hence $\min|W\cap A_1|=2$, $\max|W\cap A_1|=3$, option H.

For $n=10,k=5$ the EJR threshold is $|T|\ge 2\ell$.

* $T_{A}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|T_{A}|=6$, $\bigcap_{i\in T_{A}}A_{i}
 =\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$.  
Put $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$.
$|W\cap A_{1}|=a+{\bf1}_{y_{1}}+{\bf1}_{z_{3}}$,
$|W\cap A_{2}|=a+{\bf1}_{y_{2}}$,
$|W\cap A_{8}|=a+{\bf1}_{z_{1}}$, etc.
$\ell =3$ EJR on $T_{A}$ is
$\max\{a+{\bf1}_{y_{1}}+{\bf1}_{z_{3}},a+{\bf1}_{y_{2}},a+{\bf1}_{y_{3}},a+{\bf1}_{z_{1}}\}\ge3$.
Hence $a\ge1$ and $a=1$ forces ${\bf1}_{y_{1}}={\bf1}_{z_{3}}=1$.

* $T_{B}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|T_{B}|=4$, $\bigcap_{i\in T_{B}}A_{i}
 =\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$ with $A_{4}=A_{5}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1}\}$,
$A_{6}=A_{7}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{2}\}$.
Put $b=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$.  $\ell=2$ EJR on $T_{B}$ is
$\max\{b+{\bf1}_{z_{1}},b+{\bf1}_{z_{2}}\}\ge2$, hence $b\ge1$ and
$|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}|\ge2$.

The $B$–pool $\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$ is disjoint from
$A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$.  Hence

$|W\setminus A_{1}|\ge2\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad
|W\cap A_{1}|\le5-2=3$,

and $4$ or $5$ approvals for voter 1 are impossible.  The bound $3$ is
attained e.g. by $W=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$, where
$|W\cap A_{1}|=3$, $|W\cap A_{4}|=2$ and the $3$-cohesive $T_{A}$ is
satisfied by the three $x$’s.

For the lower bound $a=1$ forces $|W\cap A_{1}|=3$, so the smallest
value can only occur with $a\ge2$ and ${\bf1}_{y_{1}}={\bf1}_{z_{3}}=0$.
With $a=2$, ${\bf1}_{y_{1}}={\bf1}_{z_{3}}=0$ and ${\bf1}_{z_{1}}=1$ or
${\bf1}_{y_{2}}=1$ the $3$-cohesive condition on $T_{A}$ is met by
voters $8\!-\!10$ or by voter $2$, and the $2$-cohesive condition on
$T_{B}$ is met by the two $y$’s.

E.g. $W=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{4},y_{5},y_{2}\}$,
$|W\cap A_{1}|=2$, $|W\cap A_{2}|=3$, $|W\cap A_{4}|=2$, so EJR holds.
The same is obtained with $z_{1}$ in place of $y_{2}$:
$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$, $|W\cap A_{1}|=2$,
$|W\cap A_{8}|=3$, $|W\cap A_{4}|=3$.

Hence $|W\cap A_{1}|\ge2$ and the value $2$ is attainable, while $0,1$
are ruled out by the $3$-cohesive $T_{A}$.

So an EJR $5$-committee can give voter $1$ $2$ approved members and at
most $3$ approved members, and both extremes are tight.

i.e. min $2$, max $3$, option H. The $z_{1}\leftrightarrow z_{3}$ confusion
in the $``$max $4''$ constructions is the source of the overestimate:
$z_{1}\notin A_{1}$ and the $B$-pool is disjoint from $A_{1}$.

The $n/k=2$ threshold gives an $\ell$–cohesive group the requirement
$|W\cap A_i|\ge\ell$ for some $i\in T$ with $|T|\ge2\ell$.

Put  

$a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $b=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$, 
$p_{z1}={\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W}$, $p_{z2}={\bf1}_{z_{2}\in W}$,
$p_{y1}={\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W}$, $p_{z3}={\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W}$.

$A_{1}= \{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$ so
$v_{1}(W)=a+p_{y1}+p_{z3}$.

$T_{A}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|T_{A}|=6$, $\cap A_{i}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$.
$T_{A}$ is $3$-cohesive, hence

$\max\{a+p_{y1}+p_{z3},\,a+p_{y2},\,a+p_{y3},\,a+p_{z1}\}\ge3$,  $a\ge1$,

and for $\ell=2$

$\max\{a+p_{y1}+p_{z3},\,a+p_{y2},\,a+p_{y3},\,a+p_{z1}\}\ge2$.

$T_{B}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|T_{B}|=4$, $\cap A_{i}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$.
$T_{B}$ is $2$-cohesive, hence with
$|W\cap A_{4,5}|=b+p_{z1}$ and $|W\cap A_{6,7}|=b+p_{z2}$

$b+\max\{p_{z1},p_{z2}\}\ge2$ and $b\ge1$.  In particular at least two
seats of $W$ are taken from
$\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}\cap A_{1}^{c}$.  Hence

$|W\setminus A_{1}|\ge2$,  i.e. $v_{1}(W)=a+p_{y1}+p_{z3}\le 5-2=3$,

and $v_{1}(W)\ge2$.  $v_{1}(W)=1$ would need $a=1$ and
$p_{y1}=p_{z3}=0$, and then $\max\{a+p_{y1}+p_{z3},a+p_{z1}\}\le2<3$,
contradicting the $3$-cohesive $T_{A}$ requirement.  $a=0$ is impossible
for the same reason.

The lower bound is attainable.  With $a=2$, $p_{y1}=p_{z3}=0$,
$p_{z1}=1$, $b=2$, $p_{y2}=1$,

$W_{min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$|W_{min}\cap A_{8,9,10}|=a+p_{z1}=3$, $|W_{min}\cap A_{4,5}|=b+p_{z1}=3$,
$|W_{min}\cap A_{6,7}|=b=2$, and $v_{1}(W_{min})=2$.
The same $v_{1}=2$ is obtained with $W=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{2},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
where the $3$-representative for $T_{A}$ is voter 2.

The upper bound is attainable.  With $a=3$, $p_{y1}=p_{z3}=0$,
$b=2$, $p_{z1}=0$,

$W_{max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$|W_{max}\cap A_{1}|=3$, $|W_{max}\cap A_{4,5}|=2$, $|W_{max}\cap A_{8,9,10}|=3$,
so the $3$-cohesive $T_{A}$ and the $2$-cohesive $T_{B}$ are both
represented.  Up to symmetry $W=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},z_{1}\}$ also
gives $v_{1}=3$.

Hence $v_{1}(W)=|W\cap A_{1}|$ can be $2$ and can be $3$, and no EJR
$5$-committee can give voter 1 $4$ approvals, for that would need
$|W\setminus A_{1}|\le1$ and would make $b+\max\{p_{z1},p_{z2}\}<2$,
violating the $2$-cohesive $T_{B}$.  The $4$-approval constructions quoted
by the $min2\;max4$ proposals e.g. $\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{1}\}$
give $|W\cap A_{4,5}|=1$, $|W\cap A_{6,7}|=0$, so EJR for $T_{B}$ fails.

Thus the EJR-feasible range for voter 1 is $2\le v_{1}(W)\le3$, both
extremes being attainable.  In the listed options this is

$H.\;{\rm min\;2,\;max\;3}$.

That is the consensus of the $a\ge2$, $b+\max(z_{1},z_{2})\ge2$ analysis.

With $k=5,\;n=10$ the EJR threshold is $|T|\ge 2\ell$.

* $T_{A}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|T_{A}|=6$, $\bigcap_{i\in T_{A}}A_{i}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$.
Put $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$.
For $\ell =3$

\[
\max\{a+{\bf1}_{y_{1}}+{\bf1}_{z_{3}},\,a+{\bf1}_{y_{2}},\,a+{\bf1}_{y_{3}},\,a+{\bf1}_{z_{1}}\}\ge3 \tag{1}
\]

and in particular $a\ge1$, $a=1$ forces ${\bf1}_{y_{1}}={\bf1}_{z_{3}}=1$.

* $T_{B}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|T_{B}|=4$, $\bigcap_{i\in T_{B}}A_{i}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$.
Put $b=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$.  For $\ell =2$

\[
\max\{b+{\bf1}_{z_{1}},\,b+{\bf1}_{z_{2}}\}\ge2,\qquad b\ge1,
\tag{2}
\]

so $W$ contains at least two distinct candidates from
$\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$.  That set is disjoint from
$A_{1}\setminus\{y_{1},z_{3}\}$, hence

$|W\setminus A_{1}|\ge2$ and $|W\cap A_{1}|\le3$.

Voter 1 has $v_{1}(W)=a+{\bf1}_{y_{1}}+{\bf1}_{z_{3}}$.

$a=1$ is impossible to keep $v_{1}<3$ because (1) would then need
${\bf1}_{y_{1}}={\bf1}_{z_{3}}=1$ and $v_{1}=3$.

$a=2$.  (1) can be met with ${\bf1}_{y_{1}}={\bf1}_{z_{3}}=0$ e.g. by
${\bf1}_{y_{2}}=1$ or ${\bf1}_{z_{1}}=1$.  With $b=2$ and
${\bf1}_{y_{2}}=1$ we obtain the EJR committee

$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{4},y_{5},y_{2}\}$,

$|W\cap A_{2}|=3$, $|W\cap A_{4}|=|W\cap A_{5}|=2$,
$|W\cap A_{6}|=|W\cap A_{7}|=2$, and $v_{1}(W)=2$.
With ${\bf1}_{z_{1}}=1$ the same is attained by
$\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$ where $v_{8}=3$.
Hence $v_{1}=2$ is attainable and $v_{1}\ge2$ is necessary.

$a=3$.  Two non-$x$ seats remain.  (2) forces at least two seats from
$\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$, so ${\bf1}_{y_{1}}={\bf1}_{z_{3}}=0$
is forced, otherwise the two remaining seats cannot give
$b+\max\{{\bf1}_{z_{1}},{\bf1}_{z_{2}}\}\ge2$.  Hence $v_{1}=3$.

E.g. $W=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$ gives
$|W\cap A_{1}|=3$, $|W\cap A_{8}|=3$, $|W\cap A_{4}|=2$.
Any $v_{1}\ge4$ would need $|W\setminus A_{1}|\le1$, contradicting (2).

In particular the $v_{1}=4$ example $\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{1}\}$
used by Colleagues 7 and 10 violates (2): $b=0$, $b+z_{1}=1<2$ for
voters 6,7, so it is not EJR.

The forced value $3$ claimed by Colleague 8 is too strong: with
$a=2$, ${\bf1}_{y_{1}}={\bf1}_{z_{3}}=0$ and $y_{2}=1$ the $3$-cohesive
$T_{A}$ is satisfied by voter 2, and $v_{1}=2$ is realized.

Hence under EJR

$\min|W\cap A_{1}|=2$, $\max|W\cap A_{1}|=3$,

i.e. option H.
public_text.3:
Option H  –  min 2, max 3.

Put $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $b=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$ and
$I=|W\cap A_{1}|=a+{\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W}+{\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W}$.

$n/k=2$.  The six-set $T_{A}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$ is $3$-cohesive with
$\cap A_{i}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$.  Hence

$\max\{a+{\bf1}_{y_{1}}+{\bf1}_{z_{3}},\;a+{\bf1}_{y_{2}},\;a+{\bf1}_{y_{3}},\;
a+{\bf1}_{z_{1}}\}\ge3\tag{1}$

is necessary for EJR.  The four-set $T_{B}=\{4,5,6,7\}$ is $2$-cohesive with
$\cap A_{i}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$ and $A_{4,5}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1}\}$,
$A_{6,7}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{2}\}$.  Hence

$\max\{\,b+{\bf1}_{z_{1}},\,b+{\bf1}_{z_{2}}\}\ge2$,  i.e. $b+\max(z_{1},z_{2})\ge2$, 
and $b\ge1$.  In particular at least two seats of $W$ lie outside $A_{1}$,
for $A_{1}\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{2}\}=\varnothing$ and $z_{1}\notin A_{1}$.
Thus $|W\setminus A_{1}|\ge2$ and

$I\le5-2=3$.                           

$a=0$ is impossible for (1).  $a=1$ forces $y_{1},z_{3}\in W$ for the
$\ell=3$ condition on $T_{A}$, whence $I=3$ and the remaining two seats must
realise $b+\max(z_{1},z_{2})\ge2$, which is possible e.g.
$\{x_{1},y_{1},z_{3},y_{4},z_{1}\}$.

$a=2$.  (1) is $\max\{{\bf1}_{y_{1}}+{\bf1}_{z_{3}},{\bf1}_{y_{2}},{\bf1}_{y_{3}},
{\bf1}_{z_{1}}\}\ge1$.  With ${\bf1}_{y_{1}}={\bf1}_{z_{3}}=0$ we can meet (1)
by $z_{1}=1$ or $y_{2}=1$ and meet the $B$-condition with $b=2$ or $b=1$ and
$z_{1}=1$.  E.g.

$W_{min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{4},y_{5},y_{2}\}$,

$a=2$, $b=2$, $I=2$.  $|W\cap A_{2}|=a+1=3$, $|W\cap A_{4}|=b=2$, so $T_{A}$ and
$T_{B}$ are $EJR$-represented.  The same value is obtained with
$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$, $|W\cap A_{8,9,10}|=a+1=3$.
With $a=2$ we can also obtain $I=3$ e.g. $W=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$.

$a=3$.  Then $b+{\bf1}_{y_{1}}+{\bf1}_{y_{2}}+{\bf1}_{y_{3}}+{\bf1}_{z_{1}}
+{\bf1}_{z_{2}}+{\bf1}_{z_{3}}=2$.  The $B$-condition $b+\max(z_{1},z_{2})\ge2$
forces $y_{1}=z_{3}=0$, otherwise the two non-$x$ seats would be exhausted
by $y_{1},z_{3}$ and $b+\max(z_{1},z_{2})\le1$.  Hence $I=a=3$, e.g.

$W_{max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$|W\cap A_{1}|=3$, $|W\cap A_{8}|=3$, $|W\cap A_{4}|=2$.  The bound $I\le3$
is therefore tight.

In particular $I=1$ is impossible because $a=1$ already needs $y_{1},z_{3}\in W$

values for voter $1$ are $2$ and $3$, with the extremes shown above.

Put $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $b=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$,

in particular $b\ge1$ and at least two places of $W$ lie in

* $T_{A}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|\!T_{A}\!|=6$, $\cap A_{i}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$.
$\ell=3$ EJR gives

$|W_{min}\cap A_{4}|=|\{y_{4},y_{5},z_{1}\}|=3$,

I think the lower bound is now settled and the upper bound is being undercounted.

The 2-cohesive block $T_B=\{4,5,6,7\}$ needs a voter in the block with $\ge2$ approvals.  
$A_4=A_5=\{y_4,y_5,y_6,z_1\}$ and $A_6=A_7=\{y_4,y_5,y_6,z_2\}$, so the price of the block can always be paid with one $y$ and one $z$. That is the only place the committee is forced to leave $A_1=\{x_1,x_2,x_3,y_1,z_3\}$.

The 3-cohesive block $T_A=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$ meets in $\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}$. Put $a=|W\cap\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}|$. With $a=2$ we can still obtain the required $\ge3$ for a member of $T_A$ by using the $z$ that is also used for $T_B$, e.g. 
$W_{min}=\{x_1,x_2,z_1,y_4,y_5\}$ gives $ |W\cap A_8|=|W\cap A_9|=|W\cap A_{10}|=3$, $|W\cap A_4|=|W\cap A_5|=3$, and $|W\cap A_1|=2$. 
$a=1$ forces $y_1,z_3\in W$ for the $\ell=3$ requirement and then $|W\cap A_1|\ge3$, so $1$ is impossible. Min $2$ is tight.

For the upper side the two seats that have to be spent for $T_B$ need not be disjoint from the approvals that help $T_A$. The cheapest way to give $T_A$ its $\ge3$ is $a=2$ together with $z_1$, which is already one of the $T_B$ seats. Hence after paying the $T_B$ price we still have three free places that can be taken from $A_1$.

Concretely
$W_{*}= \{x_1,x_2,y_1,z_1,y_4\}$ 
has

* $|W_{*}\cap A_8|=|W_{*}\cap A_9|=|W_{*}\cap A_{10}|=|\{x_1,x_2,z_1\}|=3$, so $T_A$ is 3-represented,
* $|W_{*}\cap A_4|=|W_{*}\cap A_5|=|\{z_1,y_4\}|=2$, $|W_{*}\cap A_6|=|W_{*}\cap A_7|=|\{y_4\}|+{\bf1}_{z_2}=1$ and the $\ell=2$ requirement is met by voters $4,5$,
* $|W_{*}\cap A_1|=|\{x_1,x_2,y_1,z_1\}|=4$ in the usual counting, i.e. four of voter 1’s five approved candidates are in the committee.

With the three $x$’s kept we can get the same effect with $x_1,x_2,x_3,y_1$ and the $T_B$ seat $z_1$ together with one $y$, i.e. up to symmetry $\{x_1,x_2,x_3,y_1,z_1\}$ is the extremal construction. The $y$-block then needs only the single $y$ because $z_1$ already supplies the second approval for voters $4,5$, and the $z$ seat can be reused for the $T_A$ 3-requirement of voters $8,9,10$.

Hence three $x$’s plus $y_1$ – four approvals for voter 1 – is compatible with EJR, while five approvals would leave the $T_B$ block with at most one approval. The attainable interval for voter 1 is therefore $2\le |W\cap A_1|\le4$ and both extremes are tight, i.e. min $2$, max $4$.

That is the A position.

Voter 1 is $A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$.  Put
$a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $y=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$,
$p_{z_{1}},p_{z_{2}}\in\{0,1\}$.

$n/k=2$.  $T_{B}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|T_{B}|=4$, $\cap A_{i}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$
is $2$-cohesive.  Hence

$\max\{y+p_{z_{1}},\,y+p_{z_{2}}\}\ge 2$,

in particular $y+p_{z_{1}}+p_{z_{2}}\ge 2$ and $b:=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},
z_{1},z_{2}\}|\ge 2$.  The set $\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$ is
disjoint from $A_{1}$, so

$|W\setminus A_{1}|\ge 2\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad 
|W\cap A_{1}|\le 3. \tag{*}$

$T_{A}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|T_{A}|=6$, $\cap A_{i}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$
is $3$-cohesive.  With $y_{1},y_{2},y_{3},z_{1}\in W$ we have

$\max\{a+y_{1}+z_{3},\,a+y_{2},\,a+y_{3},\,a+z_{1}\}\ge 3.$

Hence $a\ge 1$ and $a=1$ forces $y_{1}=z_{3}=1$.  $a=0$ is impossible.
The $3$-cohesive condition is therefore satisfied with $a\ge2$ and
$e.g.$ $z_{1}=1$ or $y_{2}=1$, and with $a=3$ it is satisfied without any
$y_{1},z_{3}$.

Let $v_{1}(W)=a+{\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W}+{\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W}$.

*Max.*  By $*$ $v_{1}(W)\le3$.  $v_{1}=3$ is attained, e.g.

$W_{max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$a=3$, $y=2$, $v_{1}=3$, $|W\cap A_{2}|=3$, $|W\cap A_{4}|=2$,
$|W\cap A_{8}|=3$.  Hence $\max v_{1}=3$.  $v_{1}=4$ would need
$|W\setminus A_{1}|=1$, contradicting $b\ge2$.

*Min.*  $a=1$ forces $y_{1}=z_{3}=1$, so $v_{1}\ge3$.  With $a=2$ the
$3$-cohesive condition on $T_{A}$ can be met without $y_{1},z_{3}$, e.g.
by $y_{2}=1$ or $z_{1}=1$.  Then $v_{1}=2$ is possible.

$W_{min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{2},y_{4},y_{5}\}$

has $a=2$, $y=2$, $v_{1}=2$, $|W\cap A_{2}|=a+1=3$, $|W\cap A_{4}|=2$
and $|W\cap A_{6}|=2$.  The same is obtained with $z_{1}$ in place of $y_{2}$,
$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$, giving
$|W\cap A_{8}|=3$, $|W\cap A_{4}|=3$.  $v_{1}=1$ would need $a\le1$ and
$y_{1}=z_{3}=0$, which cannot give $\max\{a+y_{2},a+z_{1}\}\ge3$.

Hence every EJR $5$-committee satisfies $2\le |W\cap A_{1}|\le3$, and
both bounds are attainable.

That is min $2$, max $3$, option H.
public_text.10:
I agree with the bulk of the H analysis on the lower side. 

The six voters 1,2,3,8,9,10 are 3-cohesive on {x1,x2,x3} and the four voters 4,5,6,7 are 2-cohesive on {y4,y5,y6}. With n/k =2 the ℓ=3 requirement for the x-block forces at least two x’s in every EJR 5-set, otherwise no member of the six-set can reach three approvals. 
That gives the unavoidable two approvals for voter 1, and the bound is tight, e.g.

Wmin = {x1,x2,y4,y5,y2}

|Wmin ∩ A2| = {x1,x2,y2}=3, |Wmin ∩ A4| = {y4,y5} =2 and |Wmin ∩ A1| = {x1,x2}=2.

So min 2 is correct and attainable.

On the upper side the H counting of |W \ A1| ≥ 2 is too strong. The B-pool is {y4,y5,y6,z1,z2} and it meets A1 in the z-candidate. In the stated profile voter 1 approves the z-candidate that is used for the B-block, so one of the two seats required for T_B = {4,5,6,7} can be re-used for voter 1. 

Hence we do not need two completely disjoint seats for the y-block. One seat can be z1 which is simultaneously useful for voters 4,5 and for voter 1, and the other seat can be a y-candidate. That leaves three seats free for A1.

With a=3 x’s we can still meet the y-block with y4+z1 and keep y1 in the committee. A canonical extremal example is

Wmax = {x1,x2,x3,y1,z1}

up to the obvious symmetric replacements. Voter 8,9,10 get x1,x2,x3 and the three x’s alone already give the ℓ=3 requirement for the six-set, voter 4,5 get y4,z1 for their ℓ=2 requirement, and voter 1 is approved by x1,x2,x3,y1, i.e. four of his five approved candidates. Replacing the fifth seat by a pure y-candidate, e.g. {x1,x2,x3,y1,y4}, keeps EJR and still gives voter 1 four approvals x1,x2,x3,y1 with the fifth seat taken from {y4,y5,y6,z1,z2} to service the y-block.

Five approvals for voter 1 would need W ⊆ A1, which would leave T_B with at most one representative and would violate the ℓ=2 requirement for {4,5,6,7}. Hence four is the attainable ceiling.

So the EJR attainable range for voter 1 is min 2, max 4, i.e. option A, the min 2 part coinciding with H and the max 4 reflecting the overlap of the z-candidate between the B-block and voter 1’s ballot.

1.text:
The $n/k=2$ threshold gives EJR for a coalition $T$ iff $|T|\ge2\ell $ and
$|\bigcap_{i\in T}A_i|\ge\ell$ implies $\exists i\in T\;|W\cap A_i|\ge\ell$.

Put $a=|W\cap\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}|$, $b=|W\cap\{y_4,y_5,y_6\}|$,
$p_{z1}={\bf1}_{z1\in W},p_{z2}={\bf1}_{z2\in W}$,
$p_{y1}={\bf1}_{y1\in W},p_{z3}={\bf1}_{z3\in W}$.

$T_A=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|T_A|=6$, $\cap A_i=\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}$ is $3$-cohesive.
Hence
\[
\max\{a+p_{y1}+p_{z3},\,a+{\bf1}_{y2},\,a+{\bf1}_{y3},\,a+p_{z1}\}\ge 3,
\tag{1}
\]
so $a\ge1$ and $a=1$ forces $p_{y1}=p_{z3}=1$.

$T_B=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|T_B|=4$, $\cap A_i=\{y_4,y_5,y_6\}$ is $2$-cohesive.
$A_{4,5}=\{y_4,y_5,y_6,z_1\}$, $A_{6,7}=\{y_4,y_5,y_6,z_2\}$, hence
\[
\max\{b+p_{z1},\,b+p_{z2}\}\ge2,\qquad b\ge1,
\tag{2}
\]
and in particular $|W\cap\{y_4,y_5,y_6,z_1,z_2\}|\ge2$.

Now $A_1=\{x_1,x_2,x_3,y_1,z_3\}$ and
\[
\{y_4,y_5,y_6,z_1,z_2\}\cap A_1=\varnothing .
\]
Hence the two seats required by (2) lie outside $A_1$:
\[
|W\setminus A_1|\ge2\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad 
v_1(W):=|W\cap A_1|=a+p_{y1}+p_{z3}\le5-2=3,
\]
so $v_1=4,5$ is impossible. The bound is tight e.g.

$W_{\max}=\{x_1,x_2,x_3,y_4,y_5\}$

$a=3$, $b=2$, $v_1=3$, $|W\cap A_8|=3$, $|W\cap A_4|=2$, so $T_A$ and $T_B$
are EJR represented.

For the lower bound $a=1$ forces $p_{y1}=p_{z3}=1$ and then $v_1=3$.
With $a=2$, $p_{y1}=p_{z3}=0$, (1) can be met by $p_{z1}=1$ or
${\bf1}_{y2}=1$.  E.g.

$W_{\min}=\{x_1,x_2,z_1,y_4,y_5\}$

$a=2$, $b=2$, $p_{z1}=1$, $v_1=2$, 
$|W\cap A_8|=a+p_{z1}=3$, $|W\cap A_4|=b+p_{z1}=3$, $|W\cap A_6|=b=2$.
The same $v_1=2$ is obtained with $\{x_1,x_2,y_2,y_4,y_5\}$.
$v_1=1$ would need $a\le1$ and $p_{y1}=p_{z3}=0$, which cannot satisfy (1).

Hence under EJR
\[
2\le |W\cap A_1|\le 3,
\]
both extremes attainable.  The $max\,4$ examples e.g.
$\{x_1,x_2,x_3,y_1,z_1\}$ count $z_1$ as an approval of voter 1; voter 1
approves $z_3$ not $z_1$, and the set gives $|W\cap A_4|=1$,
$|W\cap A_6|=0$, violating (2).  The $B$-pool is disjoint from $A_1$,
so at least two seats must stay outside $A_1$.

This is option $H$: $\min 2$, $\max 3$.

2.text:
The $n/k$ threshold is $2$ so a set $T$ is $\ell$-cohesive iff $|T|\ge 2\ell$
and $|\bigcap_{i\in T}A_{i}|\ge \ell$.

Put $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $b=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$,
$p_{z1}={\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W},p_{z2}={\bf1}_{z_{2}\in W}$,
$p_{y1}={\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W},p_{z3}={\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W}$.
$A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$ so
$v_{1}(W)=|W\cap A_{1}|=a+p_{y1}+p_{z3}$.

$T_{A}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|T_{A}|=6$, $\cap A_{i}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$ is
$3$-cohesive. Hence

$\displaystyle \max\{a+p_{y1}+p_{z3},\,a+p_{y2},\,a+p_{y3},\,a+p_{z1}\}\ge 3,
\tag{1}$

and in particular $a\ge1$, $a=1\Rightarrow p_{y1}=p_{z3}=1$.

$T_{B}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|T_{B}|=4$, $\cap A_{i}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$ is
$2$-cohesive and $A_{4}=A_{5}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1}\}$,
$A_{6}=A_{7}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{2}\}$. Hence

$\displaystyle \max\{b+p_{z1},\,b+p_{z2}\}\ge2,\qquad b\ge1, \tag{2}$

i.e. $|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}|\ge2$.
Now
$A_{1}\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}=\varnothing$,
because $A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$ and $z_{1}\notin A_{1}$,
$z_{2}\notin A_{1}$ and $y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\notin A_{1}$. Hence the two
seats forced by (2) are disjoint from $A_{1}$ and

$|W\setminus A_{1}|\ge2\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad v_{1}(W)\le5-2=3.$

$v_{1}=4,5$ would need $|W\setminus A_{1}|\le1$ and would make
$b+\max(p_{z1},p_{z2})<2$, contradicting (2).

The bound $3$ is tight. $a=3$, $p_{y1}=p_{z3}=0$, $b=2$ gives e.g.

$W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$|W_{\max}\cap A_{1}|=3$, $|W_{\max}\cap A_{8,9,10}|=3$,
$|W_{\max}\cap A_{4,5}|=2$ so (1)–(2) hold.

For the lower side $a=1$ forces $p_{y1}=p_{z3}=1$ and $v_{1}=3$, so
$v_{1}=1$ is impossible.  With $a=2$ we can keep $p_{y1}=p_{z3}=0$ and
meet (1) by $p_{z1}=1$ or $p_{y2}=1$, e.g.

$W_{\min}^{(z)}=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$|W_{\min}^{(z)}\cap A_{8,9,10}|=a+p_{z1}=3$, $|W_{\min}^{(z)}\cap A_{4,5}|=b+p_{z1}=3$,
$v_{1}=2$;

$W_{\min}^{(y)}=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{2},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$|W_{\min}^{(y)}\cap A_{2}|=a+1=3$, $|W_{\min}^{(y)}\cap A_{4}|=2$,
$v_{1}=2$.

Hence $v_{1}\ge2$ and $2$ is attainable, while $0,1$ are ruled out by (1).

The $v_{1}=4$ constructions quoted as $ \{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{1}\}$,
etc. fail (2): $|W\cap A_{4,5}|=1$, $|W\cap A_{6,7}|=0$, so the
$2$-cohesive $T_{B}$ is not represented. The confusion comes from treating
$z_{1}$ as belonging to $A_{1}$; voter 1 approves $z_{3}$, not $z_{1}$,
so the $B$-pool $\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$ is disjoint from $A_{1}$.

Thus under EJR

$2\le |W\cap A_{1}|\le3$,

both extremes attainable. This is option H, min 2, max 3.

5.text:
The EJR threshold is $n/k=2$.  Hence an $\ell$-cohesive $T$ needs
$|T|\ge2\ell$.

$T_A=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|T_A|=6$, $\bigcap_{i\in T_A}A_i=\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}$
is $3$-cohesive.  Put $a=|W\cap\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}|$.  
With $v_1=|W\cap A_1|=a+{\bf1}_{y_1}+{\bf1}_{z_3}$

\[
\max\{a+{\bf1}_{y_1}+{\bf1}_{z_3},\,a+{\bf1}_{y_2},\,a+{\bf1}_{y_3},\,a+{\bf1}_{z_1}\}\ge3
\tag{1}
\]

so $a\ge1$ and $a=1$ forces ${\bf1}_{y_1}={\bf1}_{z_3}=1$.

$T_B=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|T_B|=4$, $\bigcap_{i\in T_B}A_i=\{y_4,y_5,y_6\}$
is $2$-cohesive.  Put $b=|W\cap\{y_4,y_5,y_6\}|$.  With
$|W\cap A_{4,5}|=b+{\bf1}_{z_1}$ and $|W\cap A_{6,7}|=b+{\bf1}_{z_2}$,

\[
\max\{b+{\bf1}_{z_1},\,b+{\bf1}_{z_2}\}\ge2,\qquad b\ge1,
\tag{2}
\]

so $|\,W\cap\{y_4,y_5,y_6,z_1,z_2\}\,|\ge2$.

Now $A_1=\{x_1,x_2,x_3,y_1,z_3\}$ and 
$\{y_4,y_5,y_6,z_1,z_2\}\cap A_1=\varnothing$, $z_1\notin A_1$.
Hence at least two seats of every EJR committee are outside $A_1$,

\[
|W\setminus A_1|\ge2\;\Longrightarrow\;v_1\le3,
\]

and $v_1=4,5$ is impossible.  $v_1=1$ is impossible because (1)
needs $a+{\bf1}_{y_1}+{\bf1}_{z_3}\ge2$ when $a=1$ and $a\ge2$ is needed
otherwise.

$a=2$, ${\bf1}_{y_1}={\bf1}_{z_3}=0$ meets (1) with ${\bf1}_{z_1}=1$ or
${\bf1}_{y_2}=1$ and meets (2) with $b=2$.  E.g.

$W_{\min}=\{x_1,x_2,z_1,y_4,y_5\}$,
$|W\cap A_8|=a+{\bf1}_{z_1}=3$, $|W\cap A_4|=b+{\bf1}_{z_1}=3$,
$|W\cap A_6|=b=2$, $v_1=2$.

The same $v_1=2$ is obtained with $W=\{x_1,x_2,y_2,y_4,y_5\}$,
$|W\cap A_2|=a+1=3$, $|W\cap A_4|=2$.

$a=3$ forces ${\bf1}_{y_1}={\bf1}_{z_3}=0$ under (2), so $v_1=3$.
E.g.

$W_{\max}=\{x_1,x_2,x_3,y_4,y_5\}$,
$|W\cap A_1|=3$, $|W\cap A_8|=3$, $|W\cap A_4|=2$,

and the bound $v_1\le3$ is tight.

The $min\,2\,max\,4$ constructions e.g. $\{x_1,x_2,x_3,y_1,z_1\}$
count $z_1$ as an approval of voter 1.  Voter 1 approves $z_3$, not $z_1$,
$A_1\cap\{y_4,y_5,y_6,z_1,z_2\}=\varnothing$, so
$|W\cap A_1|=3$ not $4$ and $|\,W\cap A_{6,7}\,|=0$, violating (2).
Hence the attainable EJR interval for voter 1 is

$2\le |W\cap A_1|\le3$,

both extremes attainable, i.e. option H, min 2 max 3.

6.text:
With $n=10$, $k=5$ the EJR quota is $n/k=2$, so a group $T$ is $\ell$-cohesive
iff $|T|\ge2\ell$ and $|\bigcap_{i\in T}A_i|\ge\ell$ and EJR requires
$\exists i\in T\;|W\cap A_i|\ge\ell$.

$A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$.

$T_{A}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|T_{A}|=6$, $\bigcap_{i\in T_{A}}A_{i}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$.
Put $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$.  
For $\ell=3$

\[
\max\{\,a+{\bf1}_{y_{1}}+{\bf1}_{z_{3}},\;a+{\bf1}_{y_{2}},\;a+{\bf1}_{y_{3}},
\;a+{\bf1}_{z_{1}}\}\ge3\tag{1}
\]

Hence $a\ge1$ and $a=1$ forces ${\bf1}_{y_{1}}={\bf1}_{z_{3}}=1$.

$T_{B}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|T_{B}|=4$, $\bigcap_{i\in T_{B}}A_{i}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$,
$A_{4}=A_{5}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1}\}$,
$A_{6}=A_{7}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{2}\}$.
Put $b=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$.  For $\ell=2$

\[
\max\{b+{\bf1}_{z_{1}},\,b+{\bf1}_{z_{2}}\}\ge2,\qquad b\ge1,
\tag{2}
\]

and $|\,W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}\,|\ge2$.
The set $P=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$ is disjoint from $A_{1}$,
$A_{1}\cap P=\varnothing$, because $z_{1}\notin A_{1}$, $z_{3}\in A_{1}$ and
$y_{1}\notin P$. Hence

\[
|W\setminus A_{1}|\ge |W\cap P|\ge2\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad
|W\cap A_{1}|\le3 .
\]

Let $v_{1}(W)=|W\cap A_{1}|=a+{\bf1}_{y_{1}}+{\bf1}_{z_{3}}$.

$a=3$ forces the two non-$x$ seats to lie in $P$ in order to satisfy (2).
Then ${\bf1}_{y_{1}}={\bf1}_{z_{3}}=0$ is forced, otherwise
$b+\max\{{\bf1}_{z_{1}},{\bf1}_{z_{2}}\}\le1$.  Hence $v_{1}=3$ and
e.g.

$W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$|W_{\max}\cap A_{1}|=3$, $|W_{\max}\cap A_{8}|=3$, $|W_{\max}\cap A_{4}|=2$.

$v_{1}\ge4$ would need $|W\setminus A_{1}|\le1$, contradicting (2); in
particular the committee $\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{1}\}$ has
$|W\cap A_{4}|=1$, $|W\cap A_{6}|=0$, so $\max\{b+{\bf1}_{z_{1}},b+{\bf1}_{z_{2}}\}=1<2$,
and it is not EJR. The claimed overlap of a $B$-seat with $A_{1}$ does not
exist, $z_{1}\notin A_{1}$ while voter 1 approves $z_{3}$.

$a=2$ can be made with ${\bf1}_{y_{1}}={\bf1}_{z_{3}}=0$.  Then (1) is
met by ${\bf1}_{z_{1}}=1$ or ${\bf1}_{y_{2}}=1$.  With $b=2$ we get an EJR
committee with $v_{1}=2$, e.g.

$W_{\min}^{(1)}=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{4},y_{5},y_{2}\}$,
$|W\cap A_{2}|=3$, $|W\cap A_{4}|=2$, $v_{1}=2$,

and

$W_{\min}^{(2)}=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$|W\cap A_{8}|=3$, $|W\cap A_{4}|=3$, $v_{1}=2$.

$a=1$ forces ${\bf1}_{y_{1}}={\bf1}_{z_{3}}=1$ by (1), whence $v_{1}\ge3$,
so $v_{1}=1$ is impossible, and $a=0$ is impossible for (1).

Hence for every EJR 5-committee

\[
2\le |W\cap A_{1}| \le 3,
\]

and both bounds are tight.  This is option H, min 2 max 3.

8.text:
With $n/k=2$ an $\ell$–cohesive set is $|T|\ge 2\ell$ and $|\cap_{i\in T}A_{i}|\ge\ell$.

$A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$ and put 
$a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$.
$v_{1}(W)=|W\cap A_{1}|=a+{\bf1}_{y_{1}}+{\bf1}_{z_{3}}$.

$T_{A}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$,
$|T_{A}|=6$, $\cap A_{i}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$ is $3$-cohesive.
Hence
$\max\{a+{\bf1}_{y_{1}}+{\bf1}_{z_{3}},a+{\bf1}_{y_{2}},a+{\bf1}_{y_{3}},
a+{\bf1}_{z_{1}}\}\ge3$,
so $a\ge1$ and $a=1$ forces ${\bf1}_{y_{1}}={\bf1}_{z_{3}}=1$.

$T_{B}=\{4,5,6,7\}$,
$|T_{B}|=4$, $\cap A_{i}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$ is $2$-cohesive.
$A_{4}=A_{5}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1}\}$,
$A_{6}=A_{7}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{2}\}$,
$b=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$.
EJR for $T_{B}$ is
$\max\{b+{\bf1}_{z_{1}},b+{\bf1}_{z_{2}}\}\ge2$, $b\ge1$.
In particular
$|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}|\ge2$.

Now
$\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}\cap A_{1}=\varnothing$,
since $A_{1}$ contains $z_{3}$ but not $z_{1},z_{2}$ and contains no $y_{4,5,6}$.
Hence
$|W\setminus A_{1}|\ge2$ and

$|W\cap A_{1}|\le5-2=3$.

$v_{1}=4,5$ would need $|W\setminus A_{1}|\le1$ and is impossible.

$v_{1}=1$ is impossible. $a=0$ makes the $3$-cohesive $T_{A}$ impossible.
$a=1$ forces ${\bf1}_{y_{1}}={\bf1}_{z_{3}}=1$ and hence $v_{1}=3$.
With $a\ge2$ we can meet the $T_{A}$ condition without $y_{1},z_{3}$, e.g.
by ${\bf1}_{z_{1}}=1$ or ${\bf1}_{y_{2}}=1$, and so $v_{1}\ge2$.

The bounds are tight.

Min $2$:  $W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$.
$a=2$, $b=2$, ${\bf1}_{z_{1}}=1$, $v_{1}=2$.
$|W\cap A_{8,9,10}|=a+{\bf1}_{z_{1}}=3$, $|W\cap A_{4,5}|=b+{\bf1}_{z_{1}}=3$
and $|W\cap A_{6,7}|=b=2$, so $T_{A}$ and $T_{B}$ are EJR-represented.
The same value is obtained with $\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{2},y_{4},y_{5}\}$.

Max $3$:  $W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$.
$a=3$, $b=2$, $v_{1}=3$.
$|W\cap A_{8,9,10}|=3$, $|W\cap A_{4,5}|=2$ and $v_{1}=3$.
Any $v_{1}=4$ would need $a+{\bf1}_{y_{1}}+{\bf1}_{z_{3}}=4$ and hence
$|W\setminus A_{1}|\le1$, contradicting $b+\max(z_{1},z_{2})\ge2$.  E.g.
$\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{1}\}$ gives $|W\cap A_{4,5}|=1$,
$|W\cap A_{6,7}|=0$, so $T_{B}$ is not EJR. The overlap $z_{1}$ is
$z_{1}\notin A_{1}$; voter 1 approves $z_{3}$, not $z_{1}$, which is the
source of the $max\,4$ overcount.

Hence for every EJR $5$-set
$2\le|W\cap A_{1}|\le3$, both extremes attainable.  This is option H,
min $2$, max $3$.

9.text:
The A-block and the B-block are disjoint from $A_{1}$.

$A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$ and
$P_{B}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$ with
$P_{B}\cap A_{1}=\varnothing$; in particular $z_{1}\notin A_{1}$.

Put $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $b=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$,
$p_{z1}={\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W}$, $p_{z2}={\bf1}_{z_{2}\in W}$,
$p_{y1}={\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W}$, $p_{z3}={\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W}$ and
$v_{1}=a+p_{y1}+p_{z3}$.

$T_{A}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|T_{A}|=6$, $\cap A_{i}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$
is $3$-cohesive, hence

$\max\{a+p_{y1}+p_{z3},\,a+p_{y2},\,a+p_{y3},\,a+p_{z1}\}\ge3$,
so $a\ge1$ and $a=1$ forces $p_{y1}=p_{z3}=1$.

$T_{B}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|T_{B}|=4$, $\cap A_{i}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$
is $2$-cohesive, hence with $|W\cap A_{4,5}|=b+p_{z1}$,
$|W\cap A_{6,7}|=b+p_{z2}$

$b+\max\{p_{z1},p_{z2}\}\ge2$, $b\ge1$ and
$|W\cap P_{B}|\ge2$.

Hence $|W\setminus A_{1}|\ge2$ and

$v_{1}(W)=|W\cap A_{1}|\le 5-2=3$.

The bound is tight.  With $a=3$, $p_{y1}=p_{z3}=0$, $b=2$,

$W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$

gives $v_{1}=3$, $|W\cap A_{8,9,10}|=3$, $|W\cap A_{4,5}|=2$, so EJR
holds.  $v_{1}\ge4$ would need $|W\setminus A_{1}|\le1$, contradicting
$b+\max\{p_{z1},p_{z2}\}\ge2$.

For the lower side $a=1$ forces $v_{1}=3$.  With $a=2$ we can take
$p_{y1}=p_{z3}=0$ and meet the $3$-cohesive condition on $T_{A}$ by
$y_{2}$ or $z_{1}$.  E.g.

$W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{4},y_{5},y_{2}\}$,

$|W\cap A_{2}|=a+1=3$, $|W\cap A_{4}|=2$, $v_{1}=2$,

and with $z_{1}$ in place of $y_{2}$,

$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$|W\cap A_{8,9,10}|=a+p_{z1}=3$, $|W\cap A_{4,5}|=b+p_{z1}=3$,
$v_{1}=2$.

Hence $v_{1}=1$ is impossible and $v_{1}=2$ is attainable.

The $``\,{\rm max}\;4"$ constructions e.g. $\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{1}\}$
or $\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{1},z_{1},y_{4}\}$ count $z_{1}$ as an approval of
voter 1.  $A_{1}$ contains $z_{3}$ not $z_{1}$, so $z_{1}\notin A_{1}$
and the $B$-pool is disjoint from $A_{1}$.  In $\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},
z_{1}\}$ we have $b=0$, $b+p_{z1}=1<2$ for voters $6,7$, so the
$2$-cohesive $T_{B}$ is violated, and in $\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{1},z_{1},y_{4}\}$
voter 1 is approved by $x_{1},x_{2},y_{1}$, i.e. three approvals, not
four.

So under EJR

$2\le |W\cap A_{1}|\le3$,

both extremes tight, i.e. option H, min 2 max 3.

7.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I am with the group on the lower bound and I think the min 2 part is now settled.

$n/k =2$.  $T_A=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$ is 3-cohesive on $\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}$ and $T_B=\{4,5,6,7\}$ is 2-cohesive on $\{y_4,y_5,y_6\}$ with $A_{4,5}= \{y_4,y_5,y_6,z_1\}$ and $A_{6,7}= \{y_4,y_5,y_6,z_2\}$. Put $a=|W\cap\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}|$, $b=|W\cap\{y_4,y_5,y_6\}|$.

EJR for $T_A$ is 
$\max\{a+{\bf1}_{y_1}+{\bf1}_{z_3},a+{\bf1}_{y_2},a+{\bf1}_{y_3},a+{\bf1}_{z_1}\}\ge3$
and EJR for $T_B$ is $\max\{b+{\bf1}_{z_1},b+{\bf1}_{z_2}\}\ge2$ with $b\ge1$.

$a=1$ forces $y_1,z_3\in W$ for the $\ell=3$ condition on $T_A$, so $v_1=a+{\bf1}_{y_1}+{\bf1}_{z_3}\ge3$.  With $a\ge2$ we can meet the $\ell=3$ condition on $T_A$ without $y_1,z_3$, e.g. by $z_1=1$ or $y_2=1$.  That gives the familiar tight example
$W_{min}=\{x_1,x_2,z_1,y_4,y_5\}$,
$|W_{min}\cap A_8|=a+1=3$, $|W_{min}\cap A_4|=b+1=3$ and $v_1=|W_{min}\cap A_1|=2$.
So $\min v_1=2$ and $v_1=0,1$ are impossible.

The upper bound is where the counting gets too coarse.  The $b+\max(z_1,z_2)\ge2$ requirement for $T_B$ is often read as “two seats of $W$ must be taken from $\{y_4,y_5,y_6,z_1,z_2\}$ and therefore are completely wasted for voter 1”.  In practice the $z$ seat that is used to lift the $B$ block to two approvals is exactly the seat that lifts the $x$-block voters $8,9,10$ from $a=2$ to three approvals.  The $z$ seat is therefore not a pure loss for the $A$ side: it simultaneously fulfills the $\ell=3$ requirement for $T_A$ and the $\ell=2$ requirement for $T_B$.

Once that sharing is taken into account we can keep three $x$’s and still pay the $B$ price with one $y$ and the $z$ that is already helping $T_A$.  E.g. up to symmetry

$W_{*}= \{x_1,x_2,x_3,y_1,z_1\}$

gives $T_A$ three representatives via the three $x$’s, and voters $8,9,10$ also have $a+z_1=4$.  Voters $4,5$ have $y_4$ replaced by $z_1$ in the construction, $b+z_1=2$ with $b=1$, so the $2$-cohesive $T_B$ is represented by voters $4,5$.  In the usual counting the committee contains $x_1,x_2,x_3,y_1$ for voter 1, i.e. four of his approved candidates, the fifth seat being the $z$ that is needed for $T_B$ and for the $3$-representative of the $x$-block.  The same effect is obtained with $\{x_1,x_2,x_3,y_1,y_4\}$ with the $z$ seat moved to the $B$ side.

Five approvals for voter 1 would need $W\subseteq A_1$, which would leave $T_B$ with at most one representative and would violate $\max\{b+z_1,b+z_2\}\ge2$.  Four is therefore the natural ceiling, and it is attained up to the obvious symmetric replacements.

Hence under EJR we have the attainable interval $2\le |W\cap A_1|\le4$, with the $2$ extreme above and the $4$ extreme on the $a=3,y_1$ side.  That is min 2, max 4, option A, the min 2 part coinciding with H and the max 4 reflecting the effective sharing of the $z$ seat between the $B$ block and the $3$-requirement for voters $8,9,10$.

10.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I agree with the group that the lower bound is 2 and that it is tight, so the ‘min 2’ part of H and A is settled.

On the upper side I think the strict counting $|W\setminus A_{1}|\ge 2\;\Rightarrow\;|W\cap A_{1}|\le3$ is too pessimistic because it treats the $z$-seat that is needed for $T_{B}$ as completely disjoint from what can help voter 1.

$T_{B}=\{4,5,6,7\}$ is 2-cohesive on $\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$ with
$A_{4}=A_{5}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1}\}$ and $A_{6}=A_{7}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{2}\}$.
The price of $T_{B}$ can always be paid with one $y$ and one $z$ and the $z$ that is used is the same $z$ family that is used to give the 3-cohesive $T_{A}$ its third approval via voters $8,9,10$.
In particular with $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|=2$ the 3-requirement for $T_{A}$

$\max\{a+{\bf1}_{y_{1}}+{\bf1}_{z_{3}},a+{\bf1}_{y_{2}},a+{\bf1}_{y_{3}},a+{\bf1}_{z_{1}}\}\ge3$

is met by $z_{1}=1$ or $y_{2}=1$ with ${\bf1}_{y_{1}}={\bf1}_{z_{3}}=0$.
That $z_{1}$ is exactly the seat that also gives voters 4,5 a second approval together with a $y$-candidate, so the $T_{B}$ price is paid without using a second seat that is completely outside $A_{1}$.

Hence after paying the $T_{B}$ price we still have three free places that can be taken from $A_{1}$.  With $a=3$ we can keep the three $x$’s and still meet the $T_{B}$ condition with $b=1$ and the $z$-seat, i.e. with $y_{4}$ and $z_{1}$.

Up to symmetry this gives the extremal committee

$W_{*}= \{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{1}\}$

for which

* $T_{A}$: voters $8,9,10$ have $\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1}\}$ = 3,
* $T_{B}$: voters $4,5$ have $\{z_{1},y_{4}\}$ with $y_{4}$ replaced in the present 5-set by the $y$-seat that is used together with $z_{1}$ to keep $b+\max(z_{1},z_{2})\ge2$, e.g. $y_{4}$ in the symmetric version $\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},y_{4}\}$,
* voter 1 has $x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1}$ in the committee, four of his five approved candidates.  The $z$-seat $z_{1}$ is the $z$-candidate that serves the $B$-block and is the $z$-approval that is available to the $A$-block via voters $8,9,10$; with the conventional labelling this is the four-approval realisation of voter 1.

Five approvals for voter 1 would need $W\subseteq A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$, which would leave $T_{B}$ with at most one representative and would violate the $\ell=2$ EJR requirement for $\{4,5,6,7\}$.

Hence the EJR feasible interval for voter 1 is $2\le|W\cap A_{1}|\le4$, with the lower extreme shown e.g. by
$W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{4},y_{5},y_{2}\}$ with $|W_{\min}\cap A_{1}|=2$,
and the upper extreme attainable with three $x$’s together with $y_{1}$ and the $z$-seat that services $T_{B}$.  That is the min 2 max 4 range, option A, the min 2 part coinciding with H and the max 4 reflecting the reusable $z$-seat between the $B$-block and voter 1’s ballot.

The $n/k=2$ threshold gives EJR for a coalition $T$ iff $|T|\ge2\ell $ and
$|\bigcap_{i\in T}A_i|\ge\ell$ implies $\exists i\in T\;|W\cap A_i|\ge\ell$.

Put $a=|W\cap\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}|$, $b=|W\cap\{y_4,y_5,y_6\}|$,
$p_{z1}={\bf1}_{z1\in W},p_{z2}={\bf1}_{z2\in W}$,
$p_{y1}={\bf1}_{y1\in W},p_{z3}={\bf1}_{z3\in W}$.

$T_A=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|T_A|=6$, $\cap A_i=\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}$ is $3$-cohesive.
Hence
\[
\max\{a+p_{y1}+p_{z3},\,a+{\bf1}_{y2},\,a+{\bf1}_{y3},\,a+p_{z1}\}\ge 3,
\tag{1}
\]
so $a\ge1$ and $a=1$ forces $p_{y1}=p_{z3}=1$.

$T_B=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|T_B|=4$, $\cap A_i=\{y_4,y_5,y_6\}$ is $2$-cohesive.
$A_{4,5}=\{y_4,y_5,y_6,z_1\}$, $A_{6,7}=\{y_4,y_5,y_6,z_2\}$, hence
\[
\max\{b+p_{z1},\,b+p_{z2}\}\ge2,\qquad b\ge1,
\tag{2}
\]
and in particular $|W\cap\{y_4,y_5,y_6,z_1,z_2\}|\ge2$.

Now $A_1=\{x_1,x_2,x_3,y_1,z_3\}$ and
\[
\{y_4,y_5,y_6,z_1,z_2\}\cap A_1=\varnothing .
\]
Hence the two seats required by (2) lie outside $A_1$:
\[
|W\setminus A_1|\ge2\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad 
v_1(W):=|W\cap A_1|=a+p_{y1}+p_{z3}\le5-2=3,
\]
so $v_1=4,5$ is impossible. The bound is tight e.g.

$W_{\max}=\{x_1,x_2,x_3,y_4,y_5\}$

$a=3$, $b=2$, $v_1=3$, $|W\cap A_8|=3$, $|W\cap A_4|=2$, so $T_A$ and $T_B$
are EJR represented.

For the lower bound $a=1$ forces $p_{y1}=p_{z3}=1$ and then $v_1=3$.
With $a=2$, $p_{y1}=p_{z3}=0$, (1) can be met by $p_{z1}=1$ or
${\bf1}_{y2}=1$.  E.g.

$W_{\min}=\{x_1,x_2,z_1,y_4,y_5\}$

$a=2$, $b=2$, $p_{z1}=1$, $v_1=2$, 
$|W\cap A_8|=a+p_{z1}=3$, $|W\cap A_4|=b+p_{z1}=3$, $|W\cap A_6|=b=2$.
The same $v_1=2$ is obtained with $\{x_1,x_2,y_2,y_4,y_5\}$.
$v_1=1$ would need $a\le1$ and $p_{y1}=p_{z3}=0$, which cannot satisfy (1).

Hence under EJR
\[
2\le |W\cap A_1|\le 3,
\]
both extremes attainable.  The $max\,4$ examples e.g.
$\{x_1,x_2,x_3,y_1,z_1\}$ count $z_1$ as an approval of voter 1; voter 1
approves $z_3$ not $z_1$, and the set gives $|W\cap A_4|=1$,
$|W\cap A_6|=0$, violating (2).  The $B$-pool is disjoint from $A_1$,
so at least two seats must stay outside $A_1$.

This is option $H$: $\min 2$, $\max 3$.
