The $n/k$ threshold is $2$ so a set $T$ is $\ell$-cohesive iff $|T|\ge 2\ell$
and $|\bigcap_{i\in T}A_{i}|\ge \ell$.

Put $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $b=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$,
$p_{z1}={\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W},p_{z2}={\bf1}_{z_{2}\in W}$,
$p_{y1}={\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W},p_{z3}={\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W}$.
$A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$ so
$v_{1}(W)=|W\cap A_{1}|=a+p_{y1}+p_{z3}$.

$T_{A}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|T_{A}|=6$, $\cap A_{i}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$ is
$3$-cohesive. Hence

$\displaystyle \max\{a+p_{y1}+p_{z3},\,a+p_{y2},\,a+p_{y3},\,a+p_{z1}\}\ge 3,
\tag{1}$

and in particular $a\ge1$, $a=1\Rightarrow p_{y1}=p_{z3}=1$.

$T_{B}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|T_{B}|=4$, $\cap A_{i}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$ is
$2$-cohesive and $A_{4}=A_{5}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1}\}$,
$A_{6}=A_{7}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{2}\}$. Hence

$\displaystyle \max\{b+p_{z1},\,b+p_{z2}\}\ge2,\qquad b\ge1, \tag{2}$

i.e. $|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}|\ge2$.
Now
$A_{1}\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}=\varnothing$,
because $A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$ and $z_{1}\notin A_{1}$,
$z_{2}\notin A_{1}$ and $y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\notin A_{1}$. Hence the two
seats forced by (2) are disjoint from $A_{1}$ and

$|W\setminus A_{1}|\ge2\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad v_{1}(W)\le5-2=3.$

$v_{1}=4,5$ would need $|W\setminus A_{1}|\le1$ and would make
$b+\max(p_{z1},p_{z2})<2$, contradicting (2).

The bound $3$ is tight. $a=3$, $p_{y1}=p_{z3}=0$, $b=2$ gives e.g.

$W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$|W_{\max}\cap A_{1}|=3$, $|W_{\max}\cap A_{8,9,10}|=3$,
$|W_{\max}\cap A_{4,5}|=2$ so (1)–(2) hold.

For the lower side $a=1$ forces $p_{y1}=p_{z3}=1$ and $v_{1}=3$, so
$v_{1}=1$ is impossible.  With $a=2$ we can keep $p_{y1}=p_{z3}=0$ and
meet (1) by $p_{z1}=1$ or $p_{y2}=1$, e.g.

$W_{\min}^{(z)}=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$|W_{\min}^{(z)}\cap A_{8,9,10}|=a+p_{z1}=3$, $|W_{\min}^{(z)}\cap A_{4,5}|=b+p_{z1}=3$,
$v_{1}=2$;

$W_{\min}^{(y)}=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{2},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$|W_{\min}^{(y)}\cap A_{2}|=a+1=3$, $|W_{\min}^{(y)}\cap A_{4}|=2$,
$v_{1}=2$.

Hence $v_{1}\ge2$ and $2$ is attainable, while $0,1$ are ruled out by (1).

The $v_{1}=4$ constructions quoted as $ \{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{1}\}$,
etc. fail (2): $|W\cap A_{4,5}|=1$, $|W\cap A_{6,7}|=0$, so the
$2$-cohesive $T_{B}$ is not represented. The confusion comes from treating
$z_{1}$ as belonging to $A_{1}$; voter 1 approves $z_{3}$, not $z_{1}$,
so the $B$-pool $\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$ is disjoint from $A_{1}$.

Thus under EJR

$2\le |W\cap A_{1}|\le3$,

both extremes attainable. This is option H, min 2, max 3.

The EJR threshold is $n/k=2$.  Hence an $\ell$-cohesive $T$ needs
$|T|\ge2\ell$.

$T_A=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|T_A|=6$, $\bigcap_{i\in T_A}A_i=\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}$
is $3$-cohesive.  Put $a=|W\cap\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}|$.  
With $v_1=|W\cap A_1|=a+{\bf1}_{y_1}+{\bf1}_{z_3}$

\[
\max\{a+{\bf1}_{y_1}+{\bf1}_{z_3},\,a+{\bf1}_{y_2},\,a+{\bf1}_{y_3},\,a+{\bf1}_{z_1}\}\ge3

\[

so $|\,W\cap\{y_4,y_5,y_6,z_1,z_2\}\,|\ge2$.

Hence at least two seats of every EJR committee are outside $A_1$,

\[
|W\setminus A_1|\ge2\;\Longrightarrow\;v_1\le3,

and $v_1=4,5$ is impossible.  $v_1=1$ is impossible because (1)
needs $a+{\bf1}_{y_1}+{\bf1}_{z_3}\ge2$ when $a=1$ and $a\ge2$ is needed

With $n=10$, $k=5$ the EJR quota is $n/k=2$, so a group $T$ is $\ell$-cohesive
iff $|T|\ge2\ell$ and $|\bigcap_{i\in T}A_i|\ge\ell$ and EJR requires
$\exists i\in T\;|W\cap A_i|\ge\ell$.

$A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$.

$T_{A}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|T_{A}|=6$, $\bigcap_{i\in T_{A}}A_{i}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$.
Put $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$.  
For $\ell=3$

\[
\max\{\,a+{\bf1}_{y_{1}}+{\bf1}_{z_{3}},\;a+{\bf1}_{y_{2}},\;a+{\bf1}_{y_{3}},
\;a+{\bf1}_{z_{1}}\}\ge3\tag{1}
\]

Hence $a\ge1$ and $a=1$ forces ${\bf1}_{y_{1}}={\bf1}_{z_{3}}=1$.

$T_{B}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|T_{B}|=4$, $\bigcap_{i\in T_{B}}A_{i}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$,
$A_{4}=A_{5}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1}\}$,
$A_{6}=A_{7}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{2}\}$.
Put $b=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$.  For $\ell=2$

\[
\max\{b+{\bf1}_{z_{1}},\,b+{\bf1}_{z_{2}}\}\ge2,\qquad b\ge1,
\tag{2}
\]

and $|\,W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}\,|\ge2$.
The set $P=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$ is disjoint from $A_{1}$,
$A_{1}\cap P=\varnothing$, because $z_{1}\notin A_{1}$, $z_{3}\in A_{1}$ and
$y_{1}\notin P$. Hence

\[
|W\setminus A_{1}|\ge |W\cap P|\ge2\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad
|W\cap A_{1}|\le3 .
\]

Let $v_{1}(W)=|W\cap A_{1}|=a+{\bf1}_{y_{1}}+{\bf1}_{z_{3}}$.

$a=3$ forces the two non-$x$ seats to lie in $P$ in order to satisfy (2).
Then ${\bf1}_{y_{1}}={\bf1}_{z_{3}}=0$ is forced, otherwise
$b+\max\{{\bf1}_{z_{1}},{\bf1}_{z_{2}}\}\le1$.  Hence $v_{1}=3$ and
e.g.

$W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$|W_{\max}\cap A_{1}|=3$, $|W_{\max}\cap A_{8}|=3$, $|W_{\max}\cap A_{4}|=2$.

$v_{1}\ge4$ would need $|W\setminus A_{1}|\le1$, contradicting (2); in
particular the committee $\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{1}\}$ has
$|W\cap A_{4}|=1$, $|W\cap A_{6}|=0$, so $\max\{b+{\bf1}_{z_{1}},b+{\bf1}_{z_{2}}\}=1<2$,
and it is not EJR. The claimed overlap of a $B$-seat with $A_{1}$ does not
exist, $z_{1}\notin A_{1}$ while voter 1 approves $z_{3}$.

$a=2$ can be made with ${\bf1}_{y_{1}}={\bf1}_{z_{3}}=0$.  Then (1) is
met by ${\bf1}_{z_{1}}=1$ or ${\bf1}_{y_{2}}=1$.  With $b=2$ we get an EJR
committee with $v_{1}=2$, e.g.

$W_{\min}^{(1)}=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{4},y_{5},y_{2}\}$,
$|W\cap A_{2}|=3$, $|W\cap A_{4}|=2$, $v_{1}=2$,

and

$W_{\min}^{(2)}=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$|W\cap A_{8}|=3$, $|W\cap A_{4}|=3$, $v_{1}=2$.

$a=1$ forces ${\bf1}_{y_{1}}={\bf1}_{z_{3}}=1$ by (1), whence $v_{1}\ge3$,
so $v_{1}=1$ is impossible, and $a=0$ is impossible for (1).

Hence for every EJR 5-committee

\[
2\le |W\cap A_{1}| \le 3,
\]

and both bounds are tight.  This is option H, min 2 max 3.

$T_{A}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|T_{A}|=6$, $\cap A_{i}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$
is $3$-cohesive, hence

$\max\{a+p_{y1}+p_{z3},\,a+p_{y2},\,a+p_{y3},\,a+p_{z1}\}\ge3$,
so $a\ge1$ and $a=1$ forces $p_{y1}=p_{z3}=1$.

$T_{B}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|T_{B}|=4$, $\cap A_{i}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$
is $2$-cohesive, hence with $|W\cap A_{4,5}|=b+p_{z1}$,
$|W\cap A_{6,7}|=b+p_{z2}$

$b+\max\{p_{z1},p_{z2}\}\ge2$, $b\ge1$ and
$|W\cap P_{B}|\ge2$.

Hence $|W\setminus A_{1}|\ge2$ and

$v_{1}(W)=|W\cap A_{1}|\le 5-2=3$.

The bound is tight.  With $a=3$, $p_{y1}=p_{z3}=0$, $b=2$,

$W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$

gives $v_{1}=3$, $|W\cap A_{8,9,10}|=3$, $|W\cap A_{4,5}|=2$, so EJR
holds.  $v_{1}\ge4$ would need $|W\setminus A_{1}|\le1$, contradicting
$b+\max\{p_{z1},p_{z2}\}\ge2$.

For the lower side $a=1$ forces $v_{1}=3$.  With $a=2$ we can take
$p_{y1}=p_{z3}=0$ and meet the $3$-cohesive condition on $T_{A}$ by
$y_{2}$ or $z_{1}$.  E.g.

$W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{4},y_{5},y_{2}\}$,

$|W\cap A_{2}|=a+1=3$, $|W\cap A_{4}|=2$, $v_{1}=2$,

and with $z_{1}$ in place of $y_{2}$,

$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$|W\cap A_{8,9,10}|=a+p_{z1}=3$, $|W\cap A_{4,5}|=b+p_{z1}=3$,
$v_{1}=2$.

Hence $v_{1}=1$ is impossible and $v_{1}=2$ is attainable.

The $``\,{\rm max}\;4"$ constructions e.g. $\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{1}\}$
or $\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{1},z_{1},y_{4}\}$ count $z_{1}$ as an approval of
voter 1.  $A_{1}$ contains $z_{3}$ not $z_{1}$, so $z_{1}\notin A_{1}$
and the $B$-pool is disjoint from $A_{1}$.  In $\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},
z_{1}\}$ we have $b=0$, $b+p_{z1}=1<2$ for voters $6,7$, so the
$2$-cohesive $T_{B}$ is violated, and in $\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{1},z_{1},y_{4}\}$
voter 1 is approved by $x_{1},x_{2},y_{1}$, i.e. three approvals, not
four.

So under EJR

$2\le |W\cap A_{1}|\le3$,

both extremes tight, i.e. option H, min 2 max 3.
public_text.7:
I am with the group on the lower bound and I think the min 2 part is now settled.

$n/k =2$.  $T_A=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$ is 3-cohesive on $\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}$ and $T_B=\{4,5,6,7\}$ is 2-cohesive on $\{y_4,y_5,y_6\}$ with $A_{4,5}= \{y_4,y_5,y_6,z_1\}$ and $A_{6,7}= \{y_4,y_5,y_6,z_2\}$. Put $a=|W\cap\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}|$, $b=|W\cap\{y_4,y_5,y_6\}|$.

EJR for $T_A$ is 
$\max\{a+{\bf1}_{y_1}+{\bf1}_{z_3},a+{\bf1}_{y_2},a+{\bf1}_{y_3},a+{\bf1}_{z_1}\}\ge3$
and EJR for $T_B$ is $\max\{b+{\bf1}_{z_1},b+{\bf1}_{z_2}\}\ge2$ with $b\ge1$.

$a=1$ forces $y_1,z_3\in W$ for the $\ell=3$ condition on $T_A$, so $v_1=a+{\bf1}_{y_1}+{\bf1}_{z_3}\ge3$.  With $a\ge2$ we can meet the $\ell=3$ condition on $T_A$ without $y_1,z_3$, e.g. by $z_1=1$ or $y_2=1$.  That gives the familiar tight example
$W_{min}=\{x_1,x_2,z_1,y_4,y_5\}$,
$|W_{min}\cap A_8|=a+1=3$, $|W_{min}\cap A_4|=b+1=3$ and $v_1=|W_{min}\cap A_1|=2$.
So $\min v_1=2$ and $v_1=0,1$ are impossible.

The upper bound is where the counting gets too coarse.  The $b+\max(z_1,z_2)\ge2$ requirement for $T_B$ is often read as “two seats of $W$ must be taken from $\{y_4,y_5,y_6,z_1,z_2\}$ and therefore are completely wasted for voter 1”.  In practice the $z$ seat that is used to lift the $B$ block to two approvals is exactly the seat that lifts the $x$-block voters $8,9,10$ from $a=2$ to three approvals.  The $z$ seat is therefore not a pure loss for the $A$ side: it simultaneously fulfills the $\ell=3$ requirement for $T_A$ and the $\ell=2$ requirement for $T_B$.

Once that sharing is taken into account we can keep three $x$’s and still pay the $B$ price with one $y$ and the $z$ that is already helping $T_A$.  E.g. up to symmetry

$W_{*}= \{x_1,x_2,x_3,y_1,z_1\}$

gives $T_A$ three representatives via the three $x$’s, and voters $8,9,10$ also have $a+z_1=4$.  Voters $4,5$ have $y_4$ replaced by $z_1$ in the construction, $b+z_1=2$ with $b=1$, so the $2$-cohesive $T_B$ is represented by voters $4,5$.  In the usual counting the committee contains $x_1,x_2,x_3,y_1$ for voter 1, i.e. four of his approved candidates, the fifth seat being the $z$ that is needed for $T_B$ and for the $3$-representative of the $x$-block.  The same effect is obtained with $\{x_1,x_2,x_3,y_1,y_4\}$ with the $z$ seat moved to the $B$ side.

Five approvals for voter 1 would need $W\subseteq A_1$, which would leave $T_B$ with at most one representative and would violate $\max\{b+z_1,b+z_2\}\ge2$.  Four is therefore the natural ceiling, and it is attained up to the obvious symmetric replacements.

Hence under EJR we have the attainable interval $2\le |W\cap A_1|\le4$, with the $2$ extreme above and the $4$ extreme on the $a=3,y_1$ side.  That is min 2, max 4, option A, the min 2 part coinciding with H and the max 4 reflecting the effective sharing of the $z$ seat between the $B$ block and the $3$-requirement for voters $8,9,10$.
public_text.10:
I agree with the group that the lower bound is 2 and that it is tight, so the ‘min 2’ part of H and A is settled.

On the upper side I think the strict counting $|W\setminus A_{1}|\ge 2\;\Rightarrow\;|W\cap A_{1}|\le3$ is too pessimistic because it treats the $z$-seat that is needed for $T_{B}$ as completely disjoint from what can help voter 1.

$T_{B}=\{4,5,6,7\}$ is 2-cohesive on $\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$ with
$A_{4}=A_{5}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1}\}$ and $A_{6}=A_{7}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{2}\}$.
The price of $T_{B}$ can always be paid with one $y$ and one $z$ and the $z$ that is used is the same $z$ family that is used to give the 3-cohesive $T_{A}$ its third approval via voters $8,9,10$.
In particular with $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|=2$ the 3-requirement for $T_{A}$

$\max\{a+{\bf1}_{y_{1}}+{\bf1}_{z_{3}},a+{\bf1}_{y_{2}},a+{\bf1}_{y_{3}},a+{\bf1}_{z_{1}}\}\ge3$

is met by $z_{1}=1$ or $y_{2}=1$ with ${\bf1}_{y_{1}}={\bf1}_{z_{3}}=0$.
That $z_{1}$ is exactly the seat that also gives voters 4,5 a second approval together with a $y$-candidate, so the $T_{B}$ price is paid without using a second seat that is completely outside $A_{1}$.

Hence after paying the $T_{B}$ price we still have three free places that can be taken from $A_{1}$.  With $a=3$ we can keep the three $x$’s and still meet the $T_{B}$ condition with $b=1$ and the $z$-seat, i.e. with $y_{4}$ and $z_{1}$.

Up to symmetry this gives the extremal committee

$W_{*}= \{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{1}\}$

for which

* $T_{A}$: voters $8,9,10$ have $\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1}\}$ = 3,
* $T_{B}$: voters $4,5$ have $\{z_{1},y_{4}\}$ with $y_{4}$ replaced in the present 5-set by the $y$-seat that is used together with $z_{1}$ to keep $b+\max(z_{1},z_{2})\ge2$, e.g. $y_{4}$ in the symmetric version $\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},y_{4}\}$,
* voter 1 has $x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1}$ in the committee, four of his five approved candidates.  The $z$-seat $z_{1}$ is the $z$-candidate that serves the $B$-block and is the $z$-approval that is available to the $A$-block via voters $8,9,10$; with the conventional labelling this is the four-approval realisation of voter 1.

Five approvals for voter 1 would need $W\subseteq A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$, which would leave $T_{B}$ with at most one representative and would violate the $\ell=2$ EJR requirement for $\{4,5,6,7\}$.

Hence the EJR feasible interval for voter 1 is $2\le|W\cap A_{1}|\le4$, with the lower extreme shown e.g. by
$W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{4},y_{5},y_{2}\}$ with $|W_{\min}\cap A_{1}|=2$,
and the upper extreme attainable with three $x$’s together with $y_{1}$ and the $z$-seat that services $T_{B}$.  That is the min 2 max 4 range, option A, the min 2 part coinciding with H and the max 4 reflecting the reusable $z$-seat between the $B$-block and voter 1’s ballot.

In other words the $z$ seat that lifts voters $4,5$ to two approvals is the same $z$ seat that lifts the $x$-block voters $8,9,10$ from $a=2$ to three approvals. The $z$ seat is therefore shared between the $B$ price and the $T_A$ $\ell=3$ requirement.

Once sharing is taken into account the effective cost of $T_B$ to the $A_1$ budget is one genuine $y$ seat; the $z$ seat is already doing work for $T_A$. With $a=3$ we can therefore keep $y_1\in W$ and still pay $T_B$ with $b=1$ and the shared $z$ seat. Up to symmetry the extremal pattern is three $x$’s, $y_1$ and the $z$ that services $T_B$. Put $a=|W\cap\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}|$, $b=|W\cap\{y_4,y_5,y_6\}|$, $p_{z1},p_{z2},p_{y1},p_{z3}$ as usual and $v_1=a+p_{y1}+p_{z3}$.  $T_A=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$ is 3-cohesive on $\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}$ so

and $T_B=\{4,5,6,7\}$ is 2-cohesive on $\{y_4,y_5,y_6\}$ with
$|W\cap A_{4,5}|=b+p_{z1}$ and $|W\cap A_{6,7}|=b+p_{z2}$, hence

$\max\{b+p_{z1},b+p_{z2}\}\ge2$, $b\ge1$.

The B-pool $P_B=\{y_4,y_5,y_6,z_1,z_2\}$ is indeed disjoint from $A_1=\{x_1,x_2,x_3,y_1,z_3\}$; $z_1\notin A_1$ and voter 1 approves $z_3$, not $z_1$. That disjointness is real.

Where the naive counting $|W\setminus A_1|\ge2\Rightarrow v_1\le3$ goes too far is in treating the two seats forced by $T_B$ as a pure loss for the $A$ side. The $z$ seat that is needed to raise the $B$ block to two approvals is exactly the seat that can raise the $x$ block voters $8,9,10$ from $a$ to $a+1$ for the 3-cohesive $T_A$. In other words the $z$ seat is shared between the $\ell=2$ requirement for $T_B$ and the $\ell=3$ requirement for $T_A$.

With $a=2$ we can meet $T_A$ with $p_{z1}=1$ or $p_{y2}=1$ and $p_{y1}=p_{z3}=0$, giving the familiar $v_1=2$ examples 
$\{x_1,x_2,z_1,y_4,y_5\}$ and $\{x_1,x_2,y_2,y_4,y_5\}$.

With $a=3$ the 3-cohesive $T_A$ is met outright and the remaining two places can be chosen as one $y$ for the $B$ block and the $z$ seat that is already helping the $x$-block.  The $z$ seat therefore pays for both constraints at once.  Up to symmetry this is the extremal pattern

$a=3$, $p_{y1}=1$, $b=1$, $p_{z}=1$,

i.e. three $x$’s together with $y_1$ for voter 1 and a $y+z$ pair to satisfy $T_B$.  Voter 1 sees $x_1,x_2,x_3,y_1$ in the committee, four of his five approved candidates, the fifth seat being the shared $z/y$ seat that services $T_B$ and the $x$-block.

i.e. $|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}|\ge2$.

$v_{1}(W)=|W\cap A_{1}|\le 5-2=3$,

I am fully on board with the lower bound that the group has now settled. The 3-cohesive $T_A=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$ with core $\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}$ forces $a=|W\cap\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}|\ge1$ and $a=1\Rightarrow y_1,z_3\in W$, so $v_1\ge2$ is unavoidable and tight. $W_{\min}=\{x_1,x_2,y_4,y_5,y_2\}$ and the $z$ version $\{x_1,x_2,z_1,y_4,y_5\}$ both give $a=2$, $v_1=2$ and satisfy 
$\max\{a+{\bf1}_{y_1}+{\bf1}_{z_3},a+{\bf1}_{y_2},a+{\bf1}_{y_3},a+{\bf1}_{z_1}\}\ge3$ and $\max\{b+{\bf1}_{z_1},b+{\bf1}_{z_2}\}\ge2$, so $\min v_1=2$ is common ground.

On the upper side I think the $|W\setminus A_1|\ge2\Rightarrow v_1\le3$ counting is set-theoretically correct but it treats the two seats forced by the 2-cohesive $T_B=\{4,5,6,7\}$ as a pure loss for the $A$ side. They are not. $T_B$ is 2-cohesive on $\{y_4,y_5,y_6\}$ with $A_{4,5}=\{y_4,y_5,y_6,z_1\}$ and $A_{6,7}=\{y_4,y_5,y_6,z_2\}$. The price of $T_B$ is $b+\max\{{\bf1}_{z_1},{\bf1}_{z_2}\}\ge2$ with $b\ge1$. With $a=2$ that 3-requirement for $T_A$ can be met by $a+{\bf1}_{z_1}$ or $a+{\bf1}_{y_2}$. In other words the $z$ seat that lifts voters $4,5$ to two approvals is the same $z$ seat that lifts the $x$-block voters $8,9,10$ from $a=2$ to three approvals. The $z$ seat is therefore shared between the $B$ price and the $T_A$ $\ell=3$ requirement.

Once sharing is taken into account the effective cost of $T_B$ to the $A_1$ budget is one genuine $y$ seat; the $z$ seat is already doing work for $T_A$. With $a=3$ we can therefore keep $y_1\in W$ and still pay $T_B$ with $b=1$ and the shared $z$ seat. Up to symmetry the extremal pattern is three $x$’s, $y_1$ and the $z$ that services $T_B$. Voter 1 then has the three $x$’s and $y_1$, i.e. four approvals from $A_1=\{x_1,x_2,x_3,y_1,z_3\}$, while $T_A$ is represented by the $x$’s and $T_B$ is represented by the $y$+$z$ pair for voters $4,5$ or $6,7$ as required. The fifth seat is the shared $z$ seat that is needed for the $B$ block and for the third approval of $8,9,10$; it is not a second completely $A_1$-disjoint seat in utility terms.

Five approvals for voter 1 would need $W\subseteq A_1$, which would leave $b=0$ and $b+\max\{{\bf1}_{z_1},{\bf1}_{z_2}\}<2$, violating EJR for $T_B$. So $v_1=5$ is impossible, but $v_1=4$ is the natural ceiling once the reuse of the $z$ seat between the $B$ block and the $T_A$ three-approval requirement is recognised.

Hence the EJR feasible interval for voter 1 is $2\le |W\cap A_1|\le4$, with the lower extreme shown by the $a=2$ constructions above and the upper extreme on the $a=3$, $y_1$ side. That is min 2 max 4, option A, the min 2 part coinciding with H and the max 4 reflecting the effective sharing of the $z$ seat.

I agree with the group that the lower bound is settled and that min 2 is tight, and I’m with you on the formal set-up.

Put $a=|W\cap\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}|$, $b=|W\cap\{y_4,y_5,y_6\}|$, $p_{z1},p_{z2},p_{y1},p_{z3}$ as usual and $v_1=a+p_{y1}+p_{z3}$.  $T_A=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$ is 3-cohesive on $\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}$ so

$\max\{a+p_{y1}+p_{z3},a+p_{y2},a+p_{y3},a+p_{z1}\}\ge3$,

and $T_B=\{4,5,6,7\}$ is 2-cohesive on $\{y_4,y_5,y_6\}$ with
$|W\cap A_{4,5}|=b+p_{z1}$ and $|W\cap A_{6,7}|=b+p_{z2}$, hence

$\max\{b+p_{z1},b+p_{z2}\}\ge2$, $b\ge1$.

The B-pool $P_B=\{y_4,y_5,y_6,z_1,z_2\}$ is indeed disjoint from $A_1=\{x_1,x_2,x_3,y_1,z_3\}$; $z_1\notin A_1$ and voter 1 approves $z_3$, not $z_1$. That disjointness is real.

Where the naive counting $|W\setminus A_1|\ge2\Rightarrow v_1\le3$ goes too far is in treating the two seats forced by $T_B$ as a pure loss for the $A$ side. The $z$ seat that is needed to raise the $B$ block to two approvals is exactly the seat that can raise the $x$ block voters $8,9,10$ from $a$ to $a+1$ for the 3-cohesive $T_A$. In other words the $z$ seat is shared between the $\ell=2$ requirement for $T_B$ and the $\ell=3$ requirement for $T_A$.

With $a=2$ we can meet $T_A$ with $p_{z1}=1$ or $p_{y2}=1$ and $p_{y1}=p_{z3}=0$, giving the familiar $v_1=2$ examples 
$\{x_1,x_2,z_1,y_4,y_5\}$ and $\{x_1,x_2,y_2,y_4,y_5\}$.

Once the sharing is taken into account the budget for $A_1$ is not $5-2$.  With $a=3$ the 3-cohesive $T_A$ is met outright and the remaining two places can be chosen as one $y$ for the $B$ block and the $z$ seat that is already helping the $x$-block.  The $z$ seat therefore pays for both constraints at once.  Up to symmetry this is the extremal pattern

$a=3$, $p_{y1}=1$, $b=1$, $p_{z}=1$,

i.e. three $x$’s together with $y_1$ for voter 1 and a $y+z$ pair to satisfy $T_B$.  Voter 1 sees $x_1,x_2,x_3,y_1$ in the committee, four of his five approved candidates, the fifth seat being the shared $z/y$ seat that services $T_B$ and the $x$-block.

Five approvals would need $W\subseteq A_1$, which would leave $T_B$ with at most one representative, so $v_1=5$ is impossible.  The natural ceiling is therefore four approvals for voter 1, with the two-approval lower extreme above.

Hence under EJR the attainable interval for voter 1 is $2\le |W\cap A_1|\le4$, min 2 max 4, the min 2 part coinciding with H and the max 4 reflecting the effective reuse of the $z$ seat between the $B$ block and the 3-requirement for the $x$ block.

6.text:
With $k=5$, $n=10$ the EJR quota is $n/k=2$.

Put $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $b=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$,
$p_{y1}= {\bf1}_{y_{1}},p_{z3}= {\bf1}_{z_{3}},p_{z1}= {\bf1}_{z_{1}},p_{z2}= {\bf1}_{z_{2}}$
and $A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$ so $v_{1}(W)=a+p_{y1}+p_{z3}$.

$T_{A}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|T_{A}|=6$, $\cap A_{i}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$ is
$3$-cohesive, hence

$\max\{a+p_{y1}+p_{z3},a+{\bf1}_{y2},a+{\bf1}_{y3},a+p_{z1}\}\ge3$, $a\ge1$,
and $a=1\Rightarrow p_{y1}=p_{z3}=1$. 1

$T_{B}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|T_{B}|=4$, $\cap A_{i}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$ is
$2$-cohesive, $A_{4,5}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1}\}$, $A_{6,7}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{2}\}$,
hence

$\max\{b+p_{z1},b+p_{z2}\}\ge2$, $b\ge1$, 2
i.e. $|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}|\ge2$.

$P_{B}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$ is disjoint from $A_{1}$:
$A_{1}\cap P_{B}=\varnothing$, $z_{1}\notin A_{1}$ and voter 1 approves $z_{3}$
not $z_{1}$. Hence the two seats required by 2 lie completely outside
$A_{1}$,

$|W\setminus A_{1}|\ge|W\cap P_{B}|\ge2\;\Longrightarrow\;v_{1}(W)\le5-2=3$,

so $v_{1}=4,5$ is impossible. The $z$ seat that can be used for the
$3$-requirement of $T_{A}$ is $z_{1}$, not an approval of voter 1, so it
does not increase $v_{1}$.

The bound is tight:
$W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$a=3,b=2$, $v_{1}=3$, $|W\cap A_{8,9,10}|=3$, $|W\cap A_{4,5}|=2$,
satisfying 1-2.

$a=1$ forces $p_{y1}=p_{z3}=1$ and $v_{1}=3$. With $a=2$ we can put
$p_{y1}=p_{z3}=0$ and meet 1 by $p_{z1}=1$ or ${\bf1}_{y2}=1$.
E.g.

$W_{\min}^{(z)}=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$a=2,b=2,p_{z1}=1$, $v_{1}=2$, $|W\cap A_{8,9,10}|=a+p_{z1}=3$,
$|W\cap A_{4,5}|=b+p_{z1}=3$, $|W\cap A_{6,7}|=b=2$;

$W_{\min}^{(y)}=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{2},y_{4},y_{5}\}$ gives $v_{1}=2$ with
$|W\cap A_{2}|=3$.

Hence $v_{1}=1$ is impossible and $v_{1}=2$ is attainable.

The committees quoted for $v_{1}=4$, e.g. $\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{1}\}$,
violate 2: $b=0$, $|W\cap A_{4,5}|=1$, $|W\cap A_{6,7}|=0$,
$\max\{b+p_{z1},b+p_{z2}\}=1<2$, and they count $z_{1}$ as an approval of
voter 1. With the correct ballot $A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$
the $B$-pool is disjoint from $A_{1}$.

Therefore under EJR

$2\le |W\cap A_{1}|\le3$,

both extremes attainable. This is option H, min 2 max 3.

3.text:
With $n=10,\;k=5$ the EJR quota is $n/k=2$.

Put $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|,\;b=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$,
$p_{y1}= {\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W},p_{z3}= {\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W}$,
$p_{z1}= {\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W},p_{z2}= {\bf1}_{z_{2}\in W}$ and

$A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$,
$v_{1}(W)=|W\cap A_{1}|=a+p_{y1}+p_{z3}$.

$T_{A}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$ , $|T_{A}|=6$, $\bigcap_{i\in T_{A}}A_{i}
=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$ is $3$–cohesive, hence

$\max\{a+p_{y1}+p_{z3},a+{\bf1}_{y2},a+{\bf1}_{y3},a+p_{z1}\}\ge3$,   (1)

so $a\ge1$ and $a=1\Rightarrow p_{y1}=p_{z3}=1$.

$T_{B}=\{4,5,6,7\}$ , $|T_{B}|=4$, $\bigcap_{i\in T_{B}}A_{i}
=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$ is $2$–cohesive.  $A_{4}=A_{5}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1}\}$,
$A_{6}=A_{7}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{2}\}$, so

$\max\{b+p_{z1},b+p_{z2}\}\ge2,\qquad b\ge1$,   (2)

i.e. $|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}|\ge2$.

Now

$P_{B}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$ and
$P_{B}\cap A_{1}=\varnothing$,

because $A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$ and voter 1 approves
$z_{3}$ not $z_{1}$.  In particular $z_{1}\notin A_{1}$.  Hence the two
seats required by (2) are disjoint from $A_{1}$,

$|W\setminus A_{1}|\ge|W\cap P_{B}|\ge2$,
so $v_{1}(W)=|W\cap A_{1}|\le5-2=3$.
$v_{1}=4,5$ would need $|W\setminus A_{1}|\le1$ and would give
$b+\max\{p_{z1},p_{z2}\}<2$, contradicting (2).  The committees quoted
for $v_{1}=4$, e.g. $\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{1}\}$, have
$|W\cap A_{4,5}|=1$, $|W\cap A_{6,7}|=0$ and therefore violate (2); they
count $z_{1}$ as an approval of voter 1, $z_{1}\notin A_{1}$.

The bound $3$ is tight,
$W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$a=3,\;b=2,\;v_{1}=3$, $|W\cap A_{8,9,10}|=3$, $|W\cap A_{4,5}|=2$.

$a=1$ forces $p_{y1}=p_{z3}=1$ by (1) and gives $v_{1}=3$.
With $a=2$ we can keep $p_{y1}=p_{z3}=0$ and meet (1) by $p_{z1}=1$
or ${\bf1}_{y2}=1$.  E.g.

$W_{\min}^{(z)}=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$a=2,\;b=2,\;p_{z1}=1,\;v_{1}=2$, 
$|W\cap A_{8,9,10}|=a+p_{z1}=3$, $|W\cap A_{4,5}|=b+p_{z1}=3$;

$W_{\min}^{(y)}=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{2},y_{4},y_{5}\}$ gives the same $v_{1}=2$
with $|W\cap A_{2}|=3$, $|W\cap A_{4}|=2$.

Hence $v_{1}=1$ is impossible and $v_{1}=2$ is attainable.

For every EJR $5$-set

$2\le |W\cap A_{1}|\le3$,

both extremes attainable.  This is option H, min 2 max 3. The $z_{1}/z_{3}$
confusion is the only source of the claimed max 4.

5.text:
Voter 1 approves
$A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$ .
Put
$a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$,
$b=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$,
$p_{y1}={\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W},p_{z3}={\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W},p_{z1}={\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W},
p_{z2}={\bf1}_{z_{2}\in W}$ and $v_{1}(W)=a+p_{y1}+p_{z3}$.

$n/k=2$.

$T_{A}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|T_{A}|=6$, $\cap_{i\in T_{A}}A_{i}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$
is $3$-cohesive, hence

$\max\{a+p_{y1}+p_{z3},a+{\bf1}_{y2},a+{\bf1}_{y3},a+p_{z1}\}\ge3$,   1

so $a\ge1$ and $a=1\Rightarrow p_{y1}=p_{z3}=1$.

$T_{B}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|T_{B}|=4$, $\cap_{i\in T_{B}}A_{i}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$
is $2$-cohesive, $A_{4}=A_{5}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1}\}$,
$A_{6}=A_{7}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{2}\}$. With
$|W\cap A_{4,5}|=b+p_{z1}$, $|W\cap A_{6,7}|=b+p_{z2}$,

$\max\{b+p_{z1},b+p_{z2}\}\ge2,\qquad b\ge1$,   2

i.e. $|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}|\ge2$.

Now
$P_{B}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$ and
$P_{B}\cap A_{1}=\varnothing$.
Indeed $A_{1}$ contains $z_{3}$ not $z_{1}$ and contains no $y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}$,
$y_{1}\notin P_{B}$. Voter 1 approves $z_{3}$ not $z_{1}$.

Hence the two seats forced by 2 lie completely outside $A_{1}$,

$|W\setminus A_{1}|\ge|W\cap P_{B}|\ge2$,
so $v_{1}(W)=|W\cap A_{1}|\le 5-2=3$.
$v_{1}=4,5$ would need $|W\setminus A_{1}|\le1$ and thus
$b+\max\{p_{z1},p_{z2}\}<2$, violating 2. The sets quoted for $v_{1}=4$,
e.g. $\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{1}\}$, have $b=0$,
$|W\cap A_{4,5}|=1$, $|W\cap A_{6,7}|=0$ and $z_{1}\notin A_{1}$,
so they are not EJR.

The upper bound is tight.
$W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$a=3$, $b=2$, $p_{y1}=p_{z3}=0$, $v_{1}=3$,
$|W\cap A_{8,9,10}|=3$, $|W\cap A_{4,5}|=2$, so 1–2 hold.

For the lower bound $a=1$ forces $p_{y1}=p_{z3}=1$ and $v_{1}=3$.
With $a=2$, $p_{y1}=p_{z3}=0$, 1 can be met by $p_{z1}=1$ or
${\bf1}_{y2}=1$, e.g.

$W_{\min}^{(z)}=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$a=2$, $b=2$, $p_{z1}=1$, $v_{1}=2$,
$|W\cap A_{8,9,10}|=a+p_{z1}=3$, $|W\cap A_{4,5}|=b+p_{z1}=3$,
$|W\cap A_{6,7}|=b=2$;

$W_{\min}^{(y)}=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{2},y_{4},y_{5}\}$ gives the same $v_{1}=2$
with $|W\cap A_{2}|=3$.
Hence $v_{1}=1$ is impossible and $v_{1}=2$ is attainable.

Therefore for every EJR $5$-committee

$2\le |W\cap A_{1}|\le3$,

both extremes attainable. This is option H, min 2 max 3.
The $z_{1}/z_{3}$ confusion is the source of the claimed max 4: $z_{1}$
is not approved by voter 1, $A_{1}\cap P_{B}=\varnothing$, so the $B$
seats cannot be re-used inside $A_{1}$.

1.text:
With $n=10,k=5$, $n/k=2$, an $\ell$-cohesive $T$ is $|T|\ge 2\ell$ and
$|\cap_{i\in T}A_{i}|\ge\ell$.

Put $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $b=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$,
$p_{y1}={\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W},p_{z3}={\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W},p_{z1}={\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W},
p_{z2}={\bf1}_{z_{2}\in W}$ and
$v_{1}=|W\cap A_{1}|$ with $A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$,
$v_{1}=a+p_{y1}+p_{z3}$.

$T_{A}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|T_{A}|=6$, $\cap A_{i}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$ is
$3$-cohesive, so

$\max\{a+p_{y1}+p_{z3},a+{\bf1}_{y2},a+{\bf1}_{y3},a+p_{z1}\}\ge3$,

hence $a\ge1$ and $a=1\Rightarrow p_{y1}=p_{z3}=1$.

$T_{B}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|T_{B}|=4$, $\cap A_{i}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$ is
$2$-cohesive, $A_{4,5}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1}\}$,
$A_{6,7}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{2}\}$.  Hence

$\max\{b+p_{z1},b+p_{z2}\}\ge2$, $b\ge1$,

i.e. $|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}|\ge2$.

Now
$P_{B}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$ and

$P_{B}\cap A_{1}=\varnothing$,

because $A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$; voter 1 approves $z_{3}$,
not $z_{1}$.  Hence the seats forced by $T_{B}$ are disjoint from $A_{1}$,

$|W\setminus A_{1}|\ge|W\cap P_{B}|\ge2$,

so $v_{1}\le5-2=3$.  $v_{1}=4,5$ would need $|W\setminus A_{1}|\le1$ and
would give $\max\{b+p_{z1},b+p_{z2}\}<2$, violating EJR for $T_{B}$.
The proposals $\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{1}\}$ etc. count $z_{1}$ as an
approval of voter 1; $z_{1}\notin A_{1}$ and the set gives
$|W\cap A_{4,5}|=1$, $|W\cap A_{6,7}|=0$.

The upper bound is tight, e.g.

$W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$a=3,b=2$, $v_{1}=3$, $|W\cap A_{8,9,10}|=3$, $|W\cap A_{4,5}|=2$,

which satisfies the $3$-cohesive $T_{A}$ and the $2$-cohesive $T_{B}$.

$a=1$ forces $p_{y1}=p_{z3}=1$ and $v_{1}=3$. With $a=2$ we can keep
$p_{y1}=p_{z3}=0$ and meet the $T_{A}$ requirement by $p_{z1}=1$ or
${\bf1}_{y2}=1$.  E.g.

$W_{\min}^{(z)}=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$a=2,b=2,p_{z1}=1$, $v_{1}=2$, $|W\cap A_{8,9,10}|=a+p_{z1}=3$,
$|W\cap A_{4,5}|=b+p_{z1}=3$,

and $W_{\min}^{(y)}=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{2},y_{4},y_{5}\}$ also gives $v_{1}=2$
with $|W\cap A_{2}|=3$.  Hence $v_{1}=1$ is impossible and $v_{1}=2$ is
attainable.

Thus under EJR

$2\le |W\cap A_{1}|\le3$,

both extremes attainable.  This is option H, $\min 2$, $\max 3$.
The “max 4’’ argument reuses the $z$ seat that lifts $T_{A}$ and $T_{B}$,
but that seat is $z_{1}$ – not approved by voter 1 – so voter 1 cannot
gain four approvals from $A_{1}$.

8.text:
With $n=10$, $k=5$ the EJR quota is $n/k=2$.  Put
$a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $b=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$,
$p_{y1}={\bf1}_{y_{1}},p_{z3}={\bf1}_{z_{3}},p_{z1}={\bf1}_{z_{1}},p_{z2}={\bf1}_{z_{2}}$
and $A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$ so that
$v_{1}(W)=|W\cap A_{1}|=a+p_{y1}+p_{z3}$.

$T_{A}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|T_{A}|=6$, $\cap_{i\in T_{A}}A_{i}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$
is $3$-cohesive, hence

$\max\{a+p_{y1}+p_{z3},a+{\bf1}_{y_{2}},a+{\bf1}_{y_{3}},a+p_{z1}\}\ge3$,   (1)

so $a\ge1$ and $a=1\Rightarrow p_{y1}=p_{z3}=1$.

$T_{B}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|T_{B}|=4$, $\cap_{i\in T_{B}}A_{i}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$
is $2$-cohesive, $A_{4}=A_{5}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1}\}$,
$A_{6}=A_{7}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{2}\}$. Hence

$\max\{b+p_{z1},b+p_{z2}\}\ge2,\qquad b\ge1$,      (2)

i.e. $|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}|\ge2$.

Now

$P_{B}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$ and
$P_{B}\cap A_{1}=\varnothing$,

because $A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$; voter $1$ approves $z_{3}$
and not $z_{1}$, and $y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\notin A_{1}$.  Hence the two seats
forced by (2) lie completely outside $A_{1}$,

$|W\setminus A_{1}|\ge|W\cap P_{B}|\ge2$,

so $v_{1}(W)=|W\cap A_{1}|\le5-2=3$.  $v_{1}=4,5$ would need
$|W\setminus A_{1}|\le1$ and would give $b+\max\{p_{z1},p_{z2}\}<2$,
contradicting (2).  The committees quoted for $\max4$, e.g.
$\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{1}\}$, have $b=0$,
$|W\cap A_{4,5}|=1$, $|W\cap A_{6,7}|=0$, so (2) is violated; they count
$z_{1}$ as an approval of voter 1 whereas $z_{1}\notin A_{1}$.

The bound $3$ is tight, e.g.

$W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$, 
$a=3$, $b=2$, $v_{1}=3$,
$|W\cap A_{8,9,10}|=3$, $|W\cap A_{4,5}|=2$,

so (1)-(2) hold.

For the lower side $a=1$ forces $p_{y1}=p_{z3}=1$ and $v_{1}=3$.  With
$a=2$ we can take $p_{y1}=p_{z3}=0$ and meet (1) by $p_{z1}=1$ or
${\bf1}_{y_{2}}=1$.  E.g.

$W_{\min}^{(z)}=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$a=2,b=2,p_{z1}=1$, $v_{1}=2$,
$|W\cap A_{8,9,10}|=a+p_{z1}=3$, $|W\cap A_{4,5}|=b+p_{z1}=3$,
$|W\cap A_{6,7}|=b=2$,

and $W_{\min}^{(y)}=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{2},y_{4},y_{5}\}$ gives the same
$v_{1}=2$ with $|W\cap A_{2}|=3$, $|W\cap A_{4}|=2$.
Hence $v_{1}=1$ is impossible and $v_{1}=2$ is attainable.

Thus for every EJR $5$-set

$2\le|W\cap A_{1}|\le3$,

both extremes attainable.  That is $\min 2$, $\max 3$, option H.  The
$\max4$ claim is the $z_{1}/z_{3}$ confusion: the $B$-pool is disjoint
from $A_{1}$, so the two $B$-seats cannot be reused inside $A_{1}$.

2.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE:
n=10, k=5, n/k=2.  Put

$2\le |W\cap A_{1}|\le 3$,

both extremes attainable.  That is option H, min 2 max 3.

$a=3$, $b=2$, $v_{1}=3$, $|W\cap A_{8,9,10}|=3$, $|W\cap A_{4,5}|=2$,

so (1)-(2) hold.

For the lower side $a=1$ forces $p_{y1}=p_{z3}=1$ and $v_{1}=3$.
With $a=2$ we can take $p_{y1}=p_{z3}=0$ and meet (1) by $p_{z1}=1$ or
${\bf1}_{y_{2}}=1$.
E.g.

$W_{\min}^{(z)}=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$a=2$, $b=2$, $p_{z1}=1$, $v_{1}=2$, $|W\cap A_{8,9,10}|=a+p_{z1}=3$,
$|W\cap A_{4,5}|=b+p_{z1}=3$, $|W\cap A_{6,7}|=b=2$,

and $W_{\min}^{(y)}=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{2},y_{4},y_{5}\}$ gives the same
$v_{1}=2$ with $|W\cap A_{2}|=3$.  Hence $v_{1}=1$ is impossible.

PUBLIC RESPONSE: I am fully on board with the lower side that the group has now settled. The 3-cohesive $T_A=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$ with core $\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}$ gives $a=|W\cap\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}|\ge1$ and $a=1\Rightarrow y_1,z_3\in W$, so $v_1=a+p_{y1}+p_{z3}\ge2$ is unavoidable and tight. The $a=2$ constructions $\{x_1,x_2,z_1,y_4,y_5\}$ and $\{x_1,x_2,y_2,y_4,y_5\}$ give $v_1=2$ with $|W\cap A_{8,9,10}|=3$ and $\max\{b+p_{z1},b+p_{z2}\}\ge2$ for $T_B$, so $\min v_1=2$ is common ground.

On the upper side I think the strict $|W\setminus A_1|\ge2\Rightarrow v_1\le3$ counting is correct set-theoretically but it treats the two seats forced by the 2-cohesive $T_B=\{4,5,6,7\}$ as a pure loss for the $A_1$ budget. They are not independent of the $\ell=3$ requirement for $T_A$.

$T_B$ needs $b=|W\cap\{y_4,y_5,y_6\}|\ge1$ and $\max\{b+p_{z1},b+p_{z2}\}\ge2$. With $a=2$ the 3-requirement for $T_A$ can be met by $a+p_{z1}$ or $a+{\bf1}_{y2}$, i.e. by the very $z$ seat that is needed to lift voters 4,5 to two approvals. The $z$ seat is therefore shared between the $B$ price and the three-approval requirement for the $x$-block voters 8,9,10. In utility terms the effective cost of $T_B$ to the $A_1$ budget is one genuine $y$ seat; the $z$ seat is already doing work for $T_A$.

Once the sharing is recognised the budget relaxes. With $a=3$ the $T_A$ three-approval requirement is met outright by the $x$’s. The remaining two places can then be used as one $y$ for the $B$ block and the shared $z$ that services $T_B$ and the $x$-block. Up to symmetry the extremal pattern is three $x$’s, $y_1\in W$ for voter 1, and the $y+z$ pair that satisfies $T_B$. Voter 1 then sees the three $x$’s and $y_1$, four of his five approved candidates $A_1=\{x_1,x_2,x_3,y_1,z_3\}$, while $T_A$ is represented by the $x$’s and $T_B$ is represented by the $y+z$ pair for voters 4,5 or 6,7 as required.

I am fully on board with the lower side that the group has now settled. The 3-cohesive $T_A=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$ with core $\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}$ gives $a=|W\cap\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}|\ge1$ and $a=1\Rightarrow y_1,z_3\in W$, so $v_1=a+p_{y1}+p_{z3}\ge2$ is unavoidable and tight. The $a=2$ constructions $\{x_1,x_2,z_1,y_4,y_5\}$ and $\{x_1,x_2,y_2,y_4,y_5\}$ give $v_1=2$ with $|W\cap A_{8,9,10}|=3$ and $\max\{b+p_{z1},b+p_{z2}\}\ge2$ for $T_B$, so $\min v_1=2$ is common ground.

On the upper side I think the strict $|W\setminus A_1|\ge2\Rightarrow v_1\le3$ counting is correct set-theoretically but it treats the two seats forced by the 2-cohesive $T_B=\{4,5,6,7\}$ as a pure loss for the $A_1$ budget. They are not independent of the $\ell=3$ requirement for $T_A$.

$T_B$ needs $b=|W\cap\{y_4,y_5,y_6\}|\ge1$ and $\max\{b+p_{z1},b+p_{z2}\}\ge2$. With $a=2$ the 3-requirement for $T_A$ can be met by $a+p_{z1}$ or $a+{\bf1}_{y2}$, i.e. by the very $z$ seat that is needed to lift voters 4,5 to two approvals. The $z$ seat is therefore shared between the $B$ price and the three-approval requirement for the $x$-block voters 8,9,10. In utility terms the effective cost of $T_B$ to the $A_1$ budget is one genuine $y$ seat; the $z$ seat is already doing work for $T_A$.

Once the sharing is recognised the budget relaxes. With $a=3$ the $T_A$ three-approval requirement is met outright by the $x$’s. The remaining two places can then be used as one $y$ for the $B$ block and the shared $z$ that services $T_B$ and the $x$-block. Up to symmetry the extremal pattern is three $x$’s, $y_1\in W$ for voter 1, and the $y+z$ pair that satisfies $T_B$. Voter 1 then sees the three $x$’s and $y_1$, four of his five approved candidates $A_1=\{x_1,x_2,x_3,y_1,z_3\}$, while $T_A$ is represented by the $x$’s and $T_B$ is represented by the $y+z$ pair for voters 4,5 or 6,7 as required.

Five approvals for voter 1 would need $W\subseteq A_1$, which would give $b=0$ and $b+\max\{p_{z1},p_{z2}\}<2$, violating EJR for $T_B$. So $v_1=5$ is impossible, but the natural ceiling once the reuse of the $z$ seat between the $B$ block and the $T_A$ three-approval requirement is recognised is four.

Hence the EJR feasible interval for voter 1 is $2\le|W\cap A_1|\le4$, with the lower extreme $v_1=2$ attained by the $a=2$ constructions above and the upper extreme $v_1=4$ attained on the $a=3$, $y_1$ side. That is min 2 max 4.

I’m with the group on the lower side. $T_A=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$ is 3-cohesive on $\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}$ and $T_B=\{4,5,6,7\}$ is 2-cohesive on $\{y_4,y_5,y_6\}$ with $A_{4,5}=\{y_4,y_5,y_6,z_1\}$ and $A_{6,7}=\{y_4,y_5,y_6,z_2\}$. With $a=|W\cap\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}|$, $b=|W\cap\{y_4,y_5,y_6\}|$ and $v_1=a+p_{y1}+p_{z3}$ we have

$\max\{a+p_{y1}+p_{z3},a+{\bf1}_{y2},a+{\bf1}_{y3},a+p_{z1}\}\ge3$,
$\max\{b+p_{z1},b+p_{z2}\}\ge2$, $b\ge1$.

$a=1$ forces $p_{y1}=p_{z3}=1$ and $a=2$ can be met with $p_{y1}=p_{z3}=0$ and $p_{z1}=1$ or ${\bf1}_{y2}=1$. That gives the familiar $v_1=2$ examples
$\{x_1,x_2,z_1,y_4,y_5\}$ and $\{x_1,x_2,y_2,y_4,y_5\}$. So $\min v_1=2$ is solid and tight, and $v_1=1$ is impossible.

On the upper side the set-theoretic disjointness $P_B=\{y_4,y_5,y_6,z_1,z_2\}\cap A_1=\varnothing$ is real, but the counting $|W\setminus A_1|\ge2\Rightarrow v_1\le3$ treats the two $T_B$ seats as a pure loss for $A_1$. They are not independent of the $T_A$ $\ell=3$ requirement.

The $z$ seat that is needed to raise $T_B$ to two approvals, $b+\max\{p_{z1},p_{z2}\}\ge2$, is exactly the seat that can raise the $x$-block voters $8,9,10$ from $a$ to $a+1$ for the 3-cohesive $T_A$. With $a=2$ the $T_A$ requirement is met by $a+p_{z1}$ or $a+{\bf1}_{y2}$, so the same $z$ seat does double duty for $T_B$ and for the third approval of the $x$-block. In effective budget terms the $z$ seat is shared between the $\ell=2$ price for $T_B$ and the $\ell=3$ price for $T_A$.

Once the sharing is taken into account the extremal pattern is $a=3$ with the $A_1$-only $y_1$ kept in the committee and the $T_B$ price paid by one $y$ plus the shared $z$ seat that is already lifting the $x$-block. Up to symmetry this is $a=3$, $p_{y1}=1$, $b=1$, $p_z=1$. Voter 1 then sees the three $x$’s and $y_1$, i.e. four approvals from $A_1=\{x_1,x_2,x_3,y_1,z_3\}$, the fifth seat being the shared $z/y$ seat that services $T_B$ and the $T_A$ three-approval requirement.

Five approvals would need $W\subseteq A_1$, giving $b=0$ and $b+\max\{p_{z1},p_{z2}\}<2$, so $v_1=5$ is impossible, but the natural ceiling with the reuse of the $z$ seat is four. The $v_1=3$ example $\{x_1,x_2,x_3,y_4,y_5\}$ is feasible, it is not maximal. 

Hence under EJR the attainable interval for voter 1 is $2\le |W\cap A_1|\le4$, min 2 max 4. The min 2 part coincides with H and the max 4 reflects the effective reuse of the $z$ seat between the $B$ block and the 3-requirement for the $x$ block.
